title: Endoscopic fenestration and Endoscope-Guided Placement of Ventriculoperitoneal Shunt with additional side holes for Multiloculated Hydrocephalus: A Technical Note
abstract: Abstract Multiloculated hydrocephalus (MLH) is characterized by multiple non-communicating cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) compartments and is associated with disproportionately high rates of shunt malfunction and revision surgery. We describe, in a stepwise technical format, an approach combining endoscopic cystoventriculostomy (inter-loculation fenestration) with endoscope-guided ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt catheter placement in an infant with multiloculated hydrocephalus. A 10-month-old male infant presented with progressive macrocephaly and developmental delay. Preoperative TORCH serology was notable for positive Rubella IgM and IgG, supporting a congenital rubella infection. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated multiple variable-sized loculated cysts (largest 30 × 39 mm) in the interhemispheric, bilateral parietal, and left temporal regions with mass effect on dilated lateral ventricles, in keeping with multiloculated hydrocephalus of probable post-infectious/congenital origin. A rigid neuroendoscope was used to sequentially fenestrate the intraventricular septa, and a single ventricular catheter, modified with additional side ports, was then advanced under direct endoscopic vision into the fenestrated common cavity. Wide endoscopic communication was established between the previously isolated loculations. A formal endoscopic third ventriculostomy was deliberately not attempted in this case because the distorted, loculated anatomy rendered safe access to the third ventricular floor unfavourable, compounded by the patient's young age and the extent of supratentorial multiloculation, which already necessitated shunt placement. The ventricular catheter tip and side holes were confirmed endoscopically to lie freely within the fenestrated cavity, away from choroid plexus and septal remnants, with free CSF drainage confirmed prior to closure. Postoperative CT confirmed marked decompression of the previously multiloculated cysts into a single residual cavity traversed by the catheter, without hemorrhage or new isolated loculation. Endoscopic fenestration combined with endoscope-guided, side-hole-modified catheter placement is a feasible and reproducible technique that allows direct, real-time confirmation of catheter position within a fenestrated common cavity. This may reduce the risk of isolated-compartment recurrence that complicates freehand or purely image-guided catheter placement in multiloculated hydrocephalus, although larger comparative series and longer follow-up are required.

title: CardioJEPA: A Framework for Holistic Cardiac Representations Through Predictive Multimodal Alignment with ECG-Preservation
abstract: Abstract The electrocardiogram (ECG) is the most widely used cardiac diagnostic tool, but it reflects cardiac structure and function only indirectly. Aligning ECG and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) representations offers a way to transfer imaging-derived structural knowledge into the ECG encoder without compromising the electrophysiological information it already carries. Contrastive learning has become the predominant approach for ECG--CMR alignment, yet the quality of the learned representation is jointly determined by the CMR target representation, the alignment objective, and the preservation of electrophysiological information unique to the ECG. We propose CardioJEPA, a predictive alignment framework built on frozen cardiac foundation models that addresses all three: a target that separates static anatomy from cardiac motion, a predictive objective that maps ECG representations onto a fixed CMR target without instance discrimination, and a preservation term that retains nearly all pre-alignment electrophysiological information. On 63,193 paired ECG--CMR recordings from the UK Biobank, CardioJEPA outperforms previous ECG--CMR alignment methods across structural, electrical, and diagnostic tasks, retains 98.6% of the ECG-unique information present before alignment, substantially reduces the modality gap relative to matched contrastive alignment, and transfers to external cohorts for structural heart disease and Chagas cardiomyopathy without task-specific training, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

title: Anatomically-Guided Attention for False Positive Reduction in Brain Tumor Segmentation
abstract: Abstract U-Net-based brain tumor segmentation can produce false positives in anatomically implausible locations, which inflate tumor volume estimates and reduce clinical trust. We investigate whether injecting an anatomical location prior into the network's attention can reduce these errors. We propose a prior informed attention gate that conditions U-Net features on empirical tumor-location prior maps computed from the training annotations, applied as a residual spatial gate at the bottleneck and at every decoder stage. Using the BRISC dataset of 2D contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI slices (glioma, meningioma and pituitary tumor), we compare the proposed model with a vanilla U-Net and a learned-gate ablation under identical training, using 3-fold cross-validation and a held-out test set of 860 images. We evaluate Dice, IoU, precision, recall, Hausdorff distance, HD95 and a dedicated far false-positive measure. The proposed model matched the baseline in Dice (0.709 versus 0.708) and showed a slightly lower but non-significant HD95 (36.5 versus 37.9 px, p = 0.26); it did not significantly reduce far false positives (49.7 versus 48.0 px, p = 0.82). A simple location prior injected through a spatial gate is therefore insufficient on BRISC, and stronger prior integration, longer training and additional datasets are needed to establish any benefit.

title: Predicting Acute Pyelonephritis With Clinical and Ultrasound Findings: Development of the Pyelo Prediction Score
abstract: Abstract Background Diagnostic uncertainty frequently complicates the assessment of suspected acute pyelonephritis (APN). We aimed to develop a bedside score combining clinical characteristics and B-mode ultrasound findings to support diagnostic stratification before contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS). Methods This prospective, single-center observational study included consecutive episodes referred to a tertiary-care ultrasound service for suspected APN. All underwent B-mode ultrasound and CEUS. The reference outcome was the final discharge diagnosis, incorporating clinical, laboratory, microbiological, and imaging findings. A seven-predictor logistic regression model was obtained. Coefficients were converted into integer points. Discrimination and threshold-specific performance were evaluated, with exploratory analysis by renal transplant status. Results Among 329 episodes, 80 (24.3%) were classified as APN. The score included cortical hypo- and hyperechogenicity, globular renal morphology, flank pain, immunosuppression, renal calculi, and arterial hypertension, with a theoretical range of − 2 to 20 points. Area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve was 0.789. At ≥ 4 points, sensitivity was 51.3% and specificity 90.0%. At ≥ 1 point, sensitivity was 90.0% and negative predictive value 91.7%; eight APN episodes remained below threshold. At ≥ 7 points, specificity was 99.2% and positive predictive value 91.7%. Apparent discrimination was 0.813 in transplant recipients and 0.784 in non-transplant patients. Conclusions The Pyelo Prediction Score showed promising discrimination in a specialist referral cohort, but low scores did not reliably exclude APN. External validation is required before using the score to guide contrast-imaging decisions.

title: Early Postoperative Trajectories for Six-Month Outcome Prediction after Endoscopic Sinus Surgery: A Leakage-Safe Comparison of Transformer and Conventional Machine-Learning Models
abstract: Abstract Early recovery after endoscopic sinus surgery may contain prognostic information that is not available preoperatively. We investigated whether trajectories measured through one postoperative month predict six-month outcomes in chronic rhinosinusitis and whether a trajectory-specific Transformer outperforms conventional models. This secondary analysis used 95 participants from a prospective randomized study (49 control; 46 biodegradable steroid-eluting stent). Predictors comprised baseline covariates and endoscopy, five-item visual analogue scale (VAS), and 22-item Sinonasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22) measurements at baseline, two weeks, and one month. Six-month continuous outcomes were predicted using repeated nested cross-validation (10 repetitions of five folds). For six-month SNOT-22 prediction from one-month data, Extra Trees achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.044 (95% CI 1.934–2.156), compared with 2.055 (1.953–2.149) for a clinically restricted ridge model and 2.624 (2.482–2.777) for the proposed EPT-Former. EPT-Former was significantly worse than the horizon-specific best comparator at every horizon (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Adding early postoperative observations improved all principal models, but tree and regularized linear models retained an advantage. Early trajectories were informative, whereas increased architectural complexity did not improve prediction in this small structured cohort. External validation is required before clinical use.

title: Targeted delivery of streptokinase based on fibrin-specific liposomes for in vivo ultrasound catheter thrombolysis
abstract: Abstract Background Thrombolytic drugs, including streptokinase (SK), are widely used in the treatment of acute thrombosis. A new fibrin-specific immunoliposomal formulation of streptokinase (LSK) for local delivery to the thrombolytic site has demonstrated a significant increase in vascular clearance compared to native SK. Objectives To assess the feasibility of improving the efficiency of fibrin-specific liposomes for SK targeted delivery in combination with the intravascular action of catheter ultrasound (US), in acute peripheral arterial thrombosis. Methods 15 adult male mongrel dogs with arterial thrombosis induced by thrombin were divided into three groups: I) US exposure; II) SC-LSC; III) SC-LSC, followed 30 min after administration by US exposure. US frequency of 25 kHz and an intensity of 48 W/cm² was delivered to the thrombosis zone using a flexible 56 cm waveguide. Assessment of hemostatic parameters included the determination of D-dimer, fibrinogen, plasminogen, and α2-antiplasmin levels. The degree of vessel lumen patency was assessed using histological morphometry. Results An in vivo experiment demonstrated the potential to significantly enhance the thrombolytic effect of a combined thrombolytic drug comprising 60% native (molecular) SK and 40% LSK, with the additional local application of low-frequency high-intensity ultrasound. The degree of thrombolysis was greatest with the combined action of ultrasound and SK-LSK (86.1%) compared to the individual use of SK-LSK drug (70.2%) and ultrasound alone (12.3%). Conclusions The introduction of US into the thrombosis zone in combination with a thrombolytic agent containing free SK and LSK ensured a high degree of thrombolysis without causing a critical increase in fibrinogenolysis, bleeding and other dangerous consequences for animals.

title: Longitudinal Alzheimer's Disease Classification from 2.5D MRI and Clinical Data via Adaptive Gated Fusion
abstract: Abstract Reliable discrimination between cognitively stable and impaired individuals remains a clinically important challenge in Alzheimer's disease (AD) assessment. Existing multimodal deep learning approaches have predominantly relied on computationally intensive 3D convolutional networks, while relatively few studies jointly model longitudinal imaging and non-imaging data or explicitly account for patient-specific modality contributions. In this work, a multimodal longitudinal framework is proposed that combines 2.5D MRI feature extraction with bidirectional LSTM-based longitudinal sequence encoding. A residual gated fusion mechanism adaptively weights imaging and clinical features for each patient, enabling joint learning of longitudinal and multimodal representations. Structural MRI and clinical data from 204 patients across three longitudinal visits from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) were evaluated using patient-level 5-fold cross-validation to prevent information leakage across visits. The proposed framework achieved a mean AUC of 0.870 ± 0.035, balanced accuracy of 0.802, sensitivity of 0.756, and specificity of 0.847, consistently outperforming unimodal baselines and alternative architectural variants. Ablation studies demonstrated that longitudinal modeling, the 2.5D representation, and residual gated fusion each contributed independently to the overall performance. Quantitative Grad-CAM analysis further revealed cross-visit spatial consistency and significantly greater medial activation in cognitively impaired individuals than in stable individuals, indicating that the model focuses on neuroanatomically plausible regions associated with neurodegenerative change. Our work underscores the potential of multimodal longitudinal deep learning to improve AD assessment while leveraging routinely collected imaging and clinical data.

title: F18 FDG PET/CT and Urinary Bladder/Urothelial Carcinoma - Diagnostic Performance and Impact on Clinical Management: an Institutional Review
abstract: Abstract Purpose: To evaluate the incremental value of [¹⁸F] FDG PET-CT over conventional imaging for staging and restaging urothelial carcinoma, its impact on clinical management, and its prognostic significance. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 53 patients with histopathologically confirmed urothelial carcinoma who underwent [¹⁸F] FDG PET/CT between February 2011 and February 2026. PET-CT findings were compared with conventional imaging to assess changes in disease stage and clinical management. Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were evaluated using Kaplan–Meier analysis. Results: The mean patient age was 60.8 years, and 94.4% had high-grade tumors. PET/CT was performed for restaging in 45 patients (85.0%) and initial staging in 8 (15.1%). Metabolically active disease was identified in 30 patients (56.6%). Compared with conventional imaging, PET/CT upstaged 9 patients (17.0%) and down staged 2 (3.7%). Management changed in 6 patients (11.3%): five were redirected to palliative systemic therapy, while one underwent potentially curative resection of a solitary FDG-avid lymph node. Among PET-positive patients, 14/30 (46.6%) died during follow-up, all with FDG-avid nodal or distant metastatic disease. Median OS was 94.0 months (95% CI, 58.0–not reached); estimated 3-year PFS and 5-year OS were 79% and 62.1%, respectively. Conclusion: 18F-FDG PET/CT improves staging and restaging of urothelial carcinoma, resulting in clinically relevant changes in patient management. FDG-positive nodal or distant metastases are associated with poorer survival, supporting its prognostic value.

title: Hybrid bias field correction scheme driving inhomogeneous image segmentation
abstract: Abstract Intensity inhomogeneity degrades segmentation quality by reducing the contrast between target and background regions. This paper introduces a segmentation method by using both multiplicative and additive bias fields to correct intensity inhomogeneity, where a soft constraint is imposed on the additive bias field for effective regulation. Especially, the proposed model introduces a Sobolev-type functional space to constrain the smoothness of the bias field and incorporates an edge detection function to enhance adaptability to inhomogeneous regions, thereby effectively suppressing bias field interference while preserving image structure. In order to overcome the nonsmooth of the proposed model, we use the iterative convolution–thresholding method (ICTM) to approximate the total variation term and then use the alternating direction method to solve it. Furthermore, we analyze the mathematical properties of the established model and the proposed method. Numerical experiments on publicly available natural and medical image datasets the proposed model exhibits excellent performance in segmentation accuracy, robustness, and sensitivity to initial contours with comparisons made against several state-of-the-art models.

title: Successful Management of Acute SMV occlusion in Pancreatic Conversion Surgery After Carbon Ion Radiotherapy: A rare complication and surgical pitfall
abstract: Abstract Background: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is often locally advanced at diagnosis, and multimodal strategies including conversion therapy are used to increase the chance of margin-negative resection. Carbon-ion radiotherapy (CIRT) enables strong local tumor control. However, the side effect of CIRT toward local vasculature has not yet been fully understood. Literatures regarding the surgical pitfall of vessel reconstruction after CIRT have barely been reported. Case presentation: A 45-year-old female initially diagnosed with locally advanced PDAC underwent 14 cycles of systemic chemotherapy followed by CIRT. After conversion, she underwent distal pancreatectomy with common hepatic artery divestment. Superior mesenteric vein (SMV) was partially trimmed due to dense adhesion between pancreas, resulting in a 1.5cm defect. The defect was repaired primarily with 5 − 0 Prolene suture. On postoperative day2, she developed high fever and rapid deterioration of liver function. Urgent contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated critical narrowing/near-occlusion of portal vein/SMV without definite thrombus. Emergent exploratory laparotomy showed severe intimal fibrosis of SMV causing luminal compromise. The SMV defect was reconstructed using patch augmentation. The patient achieved an R0 resection with final pathological finding revealing residual ductal adenocarcinoma in a fibrotic background (pT1b pN0). Her Liver function rapidly recovered after the venous reconstruction. Conclusions: This case shows a rare post-CIRT vascular complication with SMV to portal vein fibrosis causing acute hepatic ischemia after pancreatic cancer conversion surgery, which was successfully rescued with prompt patch augmentation. To avoid such complications in conversion surgery for locally advanced pancreatic cancer (LAPC), it is of crucial importance to take radiation-related vasculopathy into consideration during the manipulation of vasculature nearby to the previously CIRT-radiated area.

title: Adaptive Frequency Routing and Uncertainty-Aware Refinement for Skin Lesion Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Skin lesion boundaries are difficult to delineate when pigmentation varies, contours are irregular, or contrast with surrounding skin is weak. Frequency-aware features can help characterize these patterns, but their contributions are not always tied to the structures being segmented. We investigate task-guided frequency routing and uncertainty-based refinement in FreqConvMamba. The Adaptive Multi-band Frequency Fusion Module (AMFFM) combines spectral and contextual features using input-dependent weights. The Task-related Frequency Routing Constraint (TFRC) guides frequency selection during training using boundary spectra derived from lesion annotations. The Frequency-conditioned Uncertainty-aware Residual Refinement (FCURR) module then uses routing descriptors to calibrate decoder features and uncertainty to guide local correction of the output probability map. Evaluations cover ISIC2017, ISIC2018, and MMOTU. On 808 ISIC2018 test images, the model achieves a Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 89.62%, a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 81.20%, and a 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 8.5683 pixels. Compared with the recorded FreqConvMamba baseline, DSC and mIoU increase by 1.17 and 1.89 percentage points, respectively. DSC reaches 88.76% on ISIC2017 and 88.68% on MMOTU. Eight ablation configurations examine the effects of individual modules and their combinations.

title: Deep Learning-Based 3D Local Fibre Orientation Estimation in Composite Computed Tomography: From Volumetric Convolutions to Real-Time Direct Projection Inversion
abstract: Abstract The mechanical integrity, load-bearing efficiency, and damage tolerance of short- and continuous-fiber-reinforced polymer (SFRP/CFRP) composites depend intrinsically on their local 3D fiber-orientation distribution. While X-ray micro-computed tomography (μCT) non-destructively reveals microstructural morphology, standard volumetric extraction relies on classical 3D structure-tensor eigen-analysis. These classical approaches require dense angular projection sets (180+ views), computationally demanding Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) reconstructions, manual filter tuning, and exhibit severe degradation under Poisson photon noise. This paper introduces an end-to-end deep learning framework for local fiber orientation estimation that operates across two practical regimes: high-precision offline volumetric inspection and real-time inline scan-to-orientation inspection. To overcome the scarcity of physical CT ground truth, we develop a physics-grounded synthetic pipeline coupling directional sampling via the von Mises-Fisher (vMF) distribution (κ∈[0.5,25]) with collision-free Random Sequential Adsorption (RSA) packing (V_f∈[10%,35%]) and GPU-accelerated forward projection with realistic Poisson noise. Ground truth is formulated analytically through second-order orientation tensors, mathematically resolving the unoriented fiber director ±180^∘ sign ambiguity. We benchmark three paradigms across N=7,889 held-out sub-volume patches drawn from 150 independent composite phantoms (70/15/15 parent split): (1) classical 3D structure tensor eigen-analysis, (2) a 3D volumetric convolutional neural network (Model B), and (3) a novel Direct Projection Network (Model C) that infers 3D orientation directly from only 8 raw 2D sinogram projection views, completely bypassing 3D volumetric reconstruction. Model B achieves an overall mean angular error of 9.35 ∘ (4.78 ∘ on aligned tape; a 67% error reduction relative to the 28.27 ∘ classical baseline) at an inference throughput of 140.9 patches/s on GPU. Model C demonstrates that 3D orientation can be recovered directly from sparse 2D projection shadows with 22.57 ∘ overall error (11.35 ∘ on aligned composites), achieving 174.0 patches/s with zero reconstruction computational overhead. Furthermore, industrial tolerance evaluation demonstrates an 84.57% in-spec acceptance rate at automotive tolerance (τ≤15^∘) for Model B. This work demonstrates that deep learning provides both a superior offline alternative to classical image filtering and a viable pathway for inline, reconstruction-free composite manufacturing quality assurance.

title: MedCapVQA: A Two-Stage Explainable Framework for Medical Visual Question Answering
abstract: Abstract Medical Visual Question Answering (Med-VQA) aims to answer natural language questions about clinical images and has significant potential for diagnostic support, medical education, and improved access to expert interpretation. Most Med-VQA systems fuse image features and question embeddings directly, a mapping that is hard to learn from the few thousand question--answer pairs that medical benchmarks provide and that is usually compensated for with large-scale domain pre-training. We propose \modelname{}, a two-stage, caption-driven framework that describes the image first and answers the question second. A MedGemma captioner, adapted with parameter-efficient fine-tuning on ROCOv2, converts each medical image into a clinically meaningful caption; a BioBERT-based reasoner with dedicated caption and question encoders and question-to-caption cross-attention then predicts the answer from text alone. We evaluate \modelname{} on the closed-ended questions of the VQA-Med 2019 benchmark, training on the official training set (3,200 medical images, 12,792 question--answer pairs) and evaluating on the official validation set (500 images, 2,000 question--answer pairs), against six baselines that represent the main prior design families: a convolutional--recurrent fusion model, BioBERT and Med3D domain-adapted variants, a self-attention fusion network, a Vision Transformer model with cross-attention, and an end-to-end fine-tuned vision-language model. All models are trained under the same protocol and across training-set proportions from 5\% to 100\%, with each data-size result averaged over ten random training subsets. \modelname{} achieves the highest validation accuracy on both tasks: 81.9\% on binary (yes/no) questions, 11.6 percentage points above the strongest baseline, and 73.9\% on 71-category multiclass questions, 5.4 points above the fine-tuned vision-language model and 13.5 points above the Vision Transformer model. The vision-language model attains a higher multiclass training accuracy but lower validation accuracy compared to \modelname{} and none of the baseline models are strong on both tasks. The \modelname{} reasoner trains on a single GPU in $\sim$5 hours. These results show that converting medical images into textual captions before reasoning is an effective and resource-efficient alternative to direct multimodal fusion, and they highlight the value of intermediate semantic representations for the design of next-generation Med-VQA systems.

title: Daily CBCT-Based Repeated-Measures Analysis of Setup Reproducibility and Treatment-Course Stability of Three Positioning–Immobilization Strategies in Cervical Cancer VMAT
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate and reproducible patient positioning is essential for image-guided radiotherapy (IGRT) in cervical cancer. This study compared pretreatment setup reproducibility and treatment-course changes among three positioning–immobilization strategies using daily cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and repeated-measures analysis. Methods This retrospective study included 255 patients undergoing volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) for cervical cancer: Group A, supine positioning with vacuum-cushion immobilization (n = 100); Group B, prone positioning with an Orfit body frame and thermoplastic fixation (n = 100); and Group C, prone positioning with an individualized belly-board system (n = 55). A total of 6,255 daily pretreatment CBCT registrations were analyzed. Pre-correction translational setup deviations in the longitudinal (LNG), lateral (LAT), and vertical (VRT) directions and the corresponding three-dimensional (3D) vector magnitude were evaluated. Generalized estimating equation (GEE) models accounted for within-patient correlation, with multivariable adjustment for age, body mass index, and irradiation field extent. Patient-level sensitivity analyses, descriptive setup-related uncertainty estimates, and threshold-based reproducibility analyses requiring simultaneous attainment in all three translational directions were also performed. Results In adjusted GEE analysis, 3D vector magnitude was greater in Group B (β = 0.0647 cm; 95% CI, 0.0077–0.1217; P = 0.026) and Group C (β = 0.1038 cm; 95% CI, 0.0342–0.1734; P = 0.003) than in Group A. Treatment fraction number was positively associated with 3D vector magnitude (β = 0.0032 cm/fraction; P < 0.001), without significant group-by-fraction interactions. Patient-level sensitivity analyses supported the overall between-group pattern. Direction-specific analyses showed greater longitudinal deviations in Group B and greater vertical deviations in Group C. Under the strict patient-level criterion requiring all three absolute directional deviations to remain ≤ 0.5 cm at every available CBCT verification, attainment rates were 43.0%, 28.0%, and 12.7% in Groups A, B, and C, respectively (P < 0.001). Conclusions The three positioning–immobilization strategies exhibited distinct patterns of pre-correction setup deviations during daily CBCT-guided VMAT for cervical cancer. Supine positioning with vacuum-cushion immobilization was associated with smaller 3D setup deviations and higher descriptive threshold-attainment rates than the two prone strategies in this cohort. These findings reflect pretreatment setup reproducibility rather than isolated immobilization-device performance, post-correction treatment accuracy, or recommended clinical planning margins. Clinical trial registration Not applicable. This study was a retrospective observational analysis of routinely collected clinical data. No prospective assignment of participants to study-related interventions was performed.

title: AI-Based Particle Size Distribution Prediction from 3D Packed-Particle Tomographic Volumes: A Comparative Study with classical Watershed Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Abstract Determining the Particle Size Distribution (PSD) of granular media and powder compacts is vital across condensed matter physics, geological sciences, and materials engineering. While X-ray computed tomography (µCT) captures granular microstructure non-destructively, traditional quantitative PSD estimation relies on classical morphological segmentation (binarization, distance transform, and watershed flooding), which is computationally intensive and sensitive to contact-neck ambiguities. In this work, we investigate whether a compact 3D Convolutional Neural Network (Compact3DCNN, 300,900 parameters) can predict normalized 20-bin PSD histograms directly from unsegmented 3D grayscale volumes without intermediate particle instance extraction. Using a synthetic dataset of 60 independent non-overlapping polydisperse packed-sphere volumes (48 3 voxels) with exact analytic PSD ground truth, we benchmark the CNN against a classical 3D Euclidean distance-transform watershed baseline on an untouched, held-out test split (N = 10, 40 train / 10 validation / 10 test). On this low-to-moderate packing regime (15%–25%), the classical watershed baseline achieved superior accuracy, attaining a mean Earth Mover’s Distance (EMD) of 0.0974 ± 0.0261 voxels compared to 0.3428 ± 0.0949 voxels for the CNN (paired 95% bootstrap CI: [+0.1837, +0.3156] voxels). Measured runtime was 1.19 ± 0.27 ms per volume for the CNN on an NVIDIA RTX 3050 Laptop GPU versus 33.71 ± 7.50 ms for the watershed pipeline on an Intel CPU; however, we emphasize that this reflects disparate computing architectures rather than a controlled hardware comparison. Furthermore, comparison against an empirical training-set-mean baseline (0.6206 ± 0.2440 vx EMD on validation) confirms that the CNN learns volume-specific morphological features (0.3970 ± 0.1335 vx, a 36.0% error reduction). A controlled validation experiment evaluating direct 1D Wasserstein-1 loss training yielded substantially higher error (1.1382 ± 0.4907 vx EMD) than the primary Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence configuration, illustrating optimization challenges in cumulative L1 histogram penalties. Our findings characterize the accuracy-throughput profile in direct volumetric PSD regression and delineate key open challenges for dense granular systems.

title: TPW-YOLO for microaneurysm detection with tile-phase consistency and workload-aware ranking
abstract: Abstract Detecting microaneurysms in retinal images requires accurate localization and careful candidate selec tion when the number of false positives is limited. TPW-YOLO combines visibility-gated tile-phase consistency learning with residual candidate ranking. During training, the detector aligns predictions for the same annotated lesion across shifted tiles. At inference, the ranker uses evidence from over lapping tiles in a single grid and leaves the candidate boxes unchanged. We evaluated the method on a common image-level partition of three public retinal image sources. On 67 internal test images, sensitivity reached 43.39% at four false positives per image on test-set score-threshold curves, exceed ing the matched random-shift baseline by 1.45 percentage points. Across three training seeds at the smaller detector scale, the descriptive mean gain was 4.75 percentage points, with a sample standard deviation of 2.84 points. Candidate ranking added 0.34–0.52 ms per image. Cross-tile supervision and candidate ranking improved lesion recovery at a fixed false-positive budget in this image-level benchmark.

title: Final survival analysis and predictors of treatment discontinuation in patients aged ≥ 80 years receiving adjuvant uracil–tegafur and leucovorin for stage III colorectal cancer: The prospective phase II HiSCO-03 trial
abstract: Abstract Background In the HiSCO-03 trial of adjuvant uracil–tegafur and leucovorin in patients aged ≥ 80 years with stage III colorectal cancer, the treatment completion rate was lower than expected. This final analysis evaluated long-term outcomes and risk factors for treatment discontinuation. Methods Of 69 enrolled patients, 65 were included in the survival analysis. In exploratory analyses, skeletal muscle mass was measured on preoperative computed tomography at the third lumbar vertebra, and risk factors for discontinuation due to adverse events or patient refusal were analyzed using logistic regression in 45 patients, excluding those who discontinued treatment because of recurrence. Results The 3-year disease-free survival rate was 70.6%, and the 5-year overall, recurrence-free, and disease-free survival rates were 75.9%, 64.5%, and 61.4%, respectively. Of the 45 patients, 30 completed and 15 discontinued treatment. In multivariable analysis, female sex (odds ratio 7.75, 95% confidence interval 1.68–56.59) and low skeletal muscle mass (odds ratio 9.69, 95% confidence interval 1.84–78.11) were independent risk factors for discontinuation. Survival did not differ between patients who completed and those who discontinued treatment. Conclusions In patients aged ≥ 80 years with stage III colorectal cancer, adjuvant uracil–tegafur and leucovorin achieved a 3-year disease-free survival rate comparable to those reported in younger patients. Low skeletal muscle mass and female sex were associated with treatment discontinuation. These factors may help identify, before treatment, patients who are likely to tolerate adjuvant chemotherapy and those who need early supportive care. Trial registration jRCTs061180087 (registered 22 March 2019 retrospectively registered).

title: Artificial Intelligence–Assisted Dental Implant Brand Identification for Prosthodontic Decision Support
abstract: Abstract Background Identifying dental implant brands from radiographs is important for prosthetic treatment planning when implant records are unavailable. However, visual similarities between implant systems complicate identification. This study evaluated a hybrid framework combining deep and handcrafted radiographic features for implant brand classification. Methods A publicly available radiographic dataset was converted into 2,688 implant region-of-interest images representing BEGO, BICON, and ITI. A group-aware split assigned 2,149 images to training and 539 to testing, keeping images from the same source radiograph together. Deep learning, handcrafted feature-based, and feature fusion approaches were compared. The proposed model combined ConvNeXt-Tiny embeddings with texture, shape, and grayscale descriptors and classified the fused features using logistic regression. Performance was assessed using the McNemar test and bootstrap confidence intervals based on 1,000 resamples. Results The proposed model achieved an accuracy of 98.5%, a macro F1-score of 0.974, a macro recall of 0.979, and a macro precision of 0.969. Recall for the underrepresented BEGO class was 96.2%. The McNemar comparison was statistically significant against Swin Transformer (p = 0.0118), but not against ConvNeXt (p = 0.2891). Conclusions Combining deep and handcrafted features showed potential for identifying implant brands within this three-brand dataset and may support prosthodontic decision-making. External validation on larger, multicenter datasets covering more implant systems is required before clinical deployment.

title: A multicentre longitudinal brain metastasis imaging dataset with lesion segmentations and clinical data
abstract: Abstract Brain metastases exhibit substantial variability in lesion burden, morphology and treatment response. Longitudinal imaging linked to lesion annotations and clinical histories can support quantitative studies of this heterogeneity. We describe a multicentre dataset from seven Spanish hospitals comprising 443 patients diagnosed between 2007 and 2022, with follow-up imaging for 216 patients. The collection contains 2842 magnetic resonance image, including 1092 three dimensional (3D) contrast-enhanced T1-weighted, 833 T2-weighted and 917 FLAIR (fluid-attenuated inversion recovery) images. Semiautomatic 3D-segmentation with expert review provides annotations for 1291 unique lesions represented by 2303 lesion observations across imaging time points. Separate labels identify contrast-enhancing and non-enhancing or necrotic tumour components, and lesion identifiers are maintained during follow-up. Accompanying records describe primary tumour characteristics, treatments, imaging dates and clinical outcomes, together with acquisition metadata and 107 morphological and radiomic features. The dataset supports research on lesion detection and segmentation, longitudinal response assessment, imaging biomarkers and mathematical models of brain metastasis growth and treatment response.

title: Downhill Esophageal Varices Caused by Arteriovenous Fistula: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Esophageal varices are classified by the direction of blood flow as uphill or downhill. In downhill esophageal varices, flow is directed from the oral side toward the anal side, and the condition is uncommon, being detected in approximately 0.5% of gastroscopies. The pathogenesis of downhill esophageal varices is diverse and the underlying cause is often difficult to identify. Case presentation A 59-year-old woman was incidentally found to have severe esophageal varices during a routine health examination. She had no haematemesis or melena and no history of liver cirrhosis, and her liver function tests were normal, although she was positive for hepatitis B surface antigen. Varices involved both the proximal and the distal esophagus. Computed tomography angiography showed tortuous, dilated esophageal and gastric fundal veins together with dilated vessels in the lower neck. A first interventional angiogram showed early venous filling only; three months later, a second angiogram demonstrated a fistula between the left inferior thyroid artery and the esophageal vein, at the site of previous thyroid surgery. A diagnosis of downhill esophageal varices caused by an arteriovenous fistula was made, and the patient was followed up with comprehensive evaluation. Conclusions Downhill esophageal varices may result from an arteriovenous fistula even in the absence of superior vena cava obstruction, and are readily mistaken for uphill varices related to portal hypertension, particularly in patients with hepatitis B. Varices that predominate in the upper or middle esophagus, or that persist after a normal portal hypertension work-up, should prompt evaluation of the cervical and mediastinal vasculature.

title: CNN-Based Denoising of Industrial CT Images: A Residual-Learning Benchmark Against Classical Filters on Synthetic Phantoms
abstract: Abstract X-ray computed tomography (CT) lets engineers look inside manufactured parts without cutting them open. The catch is that the images are noisy, and the noise gets worse as the X-ray dose drops. That grain can hide the small pores and inclusions an inspector is actually looking for, and classical filters, which follow fixed rules, tend to blur the very edges they should protect. In this project, carried out with co-author Professor Mayank Goswami for course PHC-351 (Project 9, Category B), I built a fully synthetic, non-biological benchmark of 5,000 industrial phantoms (256 × 256 pixels). The phantoms have five outer shapes, bright rims, 0 to 6 dense inclusions and 0 to 9 pores, and the noise combines Poisson photon statistics with Gaussian electronic noise at three dose levels. I trained a 17-layer residual convolutional network (DnCNN, 556,096 parameters) on 4,200 images, validated it on 400, and compared it with Gaussian, median and non-local-means filters on 400 images it had never seen. DnCNN reached a mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 50.28 dB and a structural similarity (SSIM) of 0.998. For comparison, non-local means scored 45.56 dB and 0.910, the median filter 41.38 dB and 0.964, the Gaussian filter 37.44 dB and 0.857, and the noisy input 37.93 dB and 0.809. DnCNN beat the best classical filter on all 400 test images (smallest margin + 1.87 dB, mean + 4.72 dB) and at every dose level (low 48.92 dB, medium 50.06 dB, high 50.88 dB). One caveat matters: training and test noise come from the same simulator, so these numbers are a best case, and testing on real scanner data is the obvious next step.

title: RWKV-Med: A Lightweight Hybrid RWKV-Hyena Network with Axial Decoder Refinement for Skin Lesion Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Accurate segmentation of skin lesions in dermoscopic images supports computer aided melanoma diagnosis, but most accurate networks are too large for mobile or point-of-care use. We present RWKV-Med, a lightweight hierarchical encoder decoder that places two linear-complexity token mixers where each is most effective. Receptance weighted key value (RWKV) blocks, which combine a quad directional token shift with bidirectional weighted key-value aggregation, process the high-resolution early stages, whereas HyenaPixel blocks, which apply an implicitly parameterised large-kernel convolution through the fast Fourier trans form, process the low-resolution late stages. An all-MLP decoder fuses the four scales and is refined by a pointwise bottleneck module and an axial depthwise module with dual global pooling. With 0.69 million parameters and 0.55 giga floating-point operations (GFLOPs), RWKV-Med reaches a mean intersection over union (mIoU) and mean Dice coefficient (mDice) of 90.35/94.83, 84.60/91.52 and 84.95/91.76 on the ISIC2016, ISIC2017 and ISIC2018 benchmarks. It ranks first on all five metrics on ISIC2018 and has the highest mIoU averaged over the three datasets among twelve compared methods. Trained on ISIC2018 and tested without fine-tuning on PH2, it obtains the best mIoU of six models (89.60%). An ablation on ISIC2017 shows that each added component improves mIoU, by 1.10 (pointwise bottleneck), 1.61 (axial module) and 0.97 points (RWKV stages).

title: A Hybrid Deep Learning and Morphological Framework for Metal Artifact Reduction in Cone Beam Computed Tomography
abstract: Abstract The main aim of this paper is to reduce metal artifacts present in Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) images using a hybrid deep learning and morphological framework. Dental and orthopedic CBCT scans contains the metallic objects such as dental implants crowns and filling, these metallic objects produces the unwanted dark and bright patterns in the CBCT scan image, so it can affects the important anatomical or body structures present in the image such as teeth, bones and nerves. Previously many methods are used for reducing the artifacts, using those methods artifacts can be removed but important details can be blur, smooth or change in the image. To overcome this by localizing the correction method using dynamic hounsfied unit thresholding is to find the artifacts region then anatomical details are clear in the image. Inside the selected area tells where to perform the gaussian-weighted patch interpolation then using this initial correction can be corrects after this Residual U-Net can be used for further refinement finally corrects the artifacts region. This network is trained only on the masked region so original image produce at the time of considering the selected region as a hard boundary. The processing time compatible with the need of clinical use so the full pipeline runs on GPU hardware. The framework exceeded for both classical interpolation-based correction and global deep-learning baselines on PSNR and SSIM and two blinded radiologists rated it highest for artifact suppression, anatomical preservation and also diagnostic confidence for the test set of 61 clinical CBCT Scans. The final surgical results can be improved for processing the framework instead of applying the entire CBCT scan image like globally, better to apply only artifacts region i.e., mask-based correction.

title: Deep Volumetric Classification of Pore Morphology in 3D Micro-Computed Tomography of Additively Manufactured Metallic Components
abstract: Abstract Internal porosity represents a critical factor governing mechanical fatigue and failure in metal additive manufacturing (AM). In fracture mechanics, void geometry dictates local stress intensity factors; acute and elongated geometries concentrate mechanical stress significantly more than spherical voids. Consequently, automated categorization of volumetric defects into Spherical, Elongated, and Irregular morphologies from 3D X-ray micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) is essential for non-destructive evaluation. Due to experimental acquisition constraints and extreme class imbalance in physical scans (837 labeled voids: 6.45% spherical, 44.80% elongated, 48.75% irregular), we developed a procedural 3D synthetic pore generation framework to train deep convolutional architectures. While an initial 3D Convolutional Neural Network (3D CNN) achieved 99.89% validation accuracy on synthetic data, zero-shot transfer on physical scans collapsed completely to the elongated class due to detector attenuation polarity inversion and a large-void size cutoff. Recalibrating synthetic data with scanner point-spread function (PSF) blur, noise, and sub-voxel micro-radii yielded 97.83% synthetic accuracy, yet exhibited a secondary mode collapse on physical scans due to ambient background air saturation along hollow tube boundaries. Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) diagnostics identified an order-of-magnitude volume scale mismatch between synthetic models (mean 67.51 voxels) and real defects (mean 6.76 voxels). A controlled 5-experiment ablation benchmark (Exp A–E) on a locked real held-out test set (N = 126, seed = 42) demonstrated that synthetic pretraining yielded no performance gain (42.86%) relative to training from scratch on physical scans (45.24%). Conversely, a classical Random Forest trained on mathematical geometric descriptors achieved 99.21% accuracy, confirming ground-truth label separability and establishing that raw-voxel 3D CNNs are fundamentally constrained by spatial discretization limits (53.6 μm/voxel). We propose a hybrid multi-modal feature fusion architecture bridging raw volumetric representations with classical geometric invariants for robust industrial deployment.

title: Autoencoder–Graph Neural Network Framework for Robust 3D Pore Connectivity Classification in Noisy Volumetric Images
abstract: Abstract Pore connectivity is a critical property governing the transport of fluids, gases, and ions in porous materials. Connectivity is often inferred from micro-computed tomography (μCT) volumes through thresholding and connected-component analysis. However, this pipeline is sensitive to noise and limited resolution, producing both false connections and missed links. This study investigates whether graph-based learning, using geometric features and 3D image representations, can correct such errors. We generate 250 synthetic 128³-voxel phantoms with known ground-truth connectivity, degrade them using point-spread blur and noise, and evaluate ten models spanning classical machine learning, 3D CNNs, GCN, GraphSAGE, and autoencoder–GNN fusion. The best-performing models (GraphSAGE and AE+GraphSAGE) achieve F1 scores of 0.954 and 0.957, respectively, compared with 0.468 for the raw connected-component baseline. Improvements are driven primarily by geometric features, including neck width, centroid distance, and pore volume, while frozen autoencoder embeddings provide negligible benefit. However, improved edge classification does not consistently translate into better cluster agreement or percolation prediction.

title: A Robust Evaluation of Low-Dose CT Reconstruction Through Generative and Discriminative Models
abstract: Abstract Low-dose CT (LDCT) reconstruction is a critical problem in radiology that has a significant impact on public health. With the rise of deep learning, especially in generative models, we have seen a diverse range of methods for reconstructing LDCT images. However, existing LDCT reconstruction methods are often evaluated under inconsistent experimental settings, including different dataset splits, preprocessing pipelines, and noise-generation procedures, hindering fair comparisons across approaches. In addition, many studies do not explicitly assess 1 generalization across diverse datasets with different acquisition characteristics, limiting the practical relevance of the reported results. Therefore, we present a comprehensive fair study of modern generative models for LDCT reconstructions. Beyond effectiveness on a single dataset, our main goal is to assess the models’ generalization across datasets. Moreover, we propose a new semantic segmentation-based metric, in addition to traditional image quality metrics, to evaluate the effectiveness of the reconstructed images in a medical task. Our results show that diffusion-based models with a small number of iterations out-perform UNet and GAN, especially on out-of-distribution datasets. However, there are still challenges that require further study regarding effectiveness and efficiency.

title: Improving specificity in high-sensitivity NSCLC PET/CT nodal classification with patient-specific metabolic context
abstract: Abstract Background High-sensitivity [18F]FDG-PET/CT assessment of thoracic lymph nodes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) can generate false-positive classifications when benign inflammatory uptake resembles metastatic disease. We investigated whether interpreting each nodal station within the patient's wider intrathoracic metabolic pattern can refine decisions based on local SUVmax alone. Methods We retrospectively studied 486 patients and 1,111 pathology-confirmed outcomes at six hilar or mediastinal nodal stations. Each station was assessed using local SUVmax-only logistic regression or contextual models incorporating uptake in other nodal stations, mediastinal blood-pool activity, primary-tumor uptake and laterality, and recorded inflammatory variables. Elastic-net logistic regression (EN), histogram gradient boosting, and radial-basis support-vector machines underwent ten repetitions of patient-grouped nested cross-validation. Thresholds targeting 90% or 95% sensitivity were selected from training data and transferred unchanged to held-out patients. An EN-versus-SUVmax global operating-point analysis was performed post hoc. Results At the 95% training-derived sensitivity target, an exploratory pooled comparison showed higher specificity with contextual elastic-net modeling than with SUVmax-only logistic regression (82.48% vs 78.20%; difference + 4.28 percentage points; conditional 95% confidence interval [CI] + 1.86 to + 6.76). Positive predictive value increased from 75.66% to 79.31% (+ 3.65 points; CI + 1.47 to + 5.97), while achieved sensitivity was 94.20% versus 95.13% (-0.93 points; CI -2.36 to + 0.45). Equal-station averaging supported the same pattern. The specificity gain was concentrated at the more stringent operating target. Conclusions Integrating intrathoracic metabolic measurements already available on routine PET/CT yielded more specific nodal classification under a stringent high-sensitivity operating rule. These results identify a practical opportunity for context-aware station assessment alongside local SUVmax and provide a clear basis for independent clinical validation.

title: Deep learning-based treatment suggestion on periapical radiographs in paediatric dentistry: a comparative evaluation of YOLOv11 and YOLO26
abstract: Abstract To compare YOLOv11 and YOLO26 instance segmentation models for suggesting management categories from paediatric periapical radiographs. From a single centre, 3825 periapical radiographs of children aged 3–13 years were annotated with 8 management categories assignable from radiographs alone: restoration, restoration replacement, pulp capping, pulpotomy, root canal treatment, root canal retreatment, extraction and follow-up. Teeth with 2 equally acceptable categories received dual labels. Interobserver agreement was high (mean Cohen’s kappa, 0.865). Confidence thresholds were selected on the validation set; the primary outcome, test-set macro-averaged F1-score, was compared with a paired bootstrap. The macro-averaged F1-score (95% confidence interval) was 0.610 (0.571–0.643) for YOLOv11 and 0.595 (0.553–0.632) for YOLO26, with no clear difference (− 0.014 [− 0.052 to 0.024]); YOLO26 had higher precision and lower recall. F1-scores were highest for extraction (0.805 and 0.780) and lowest for restoration replacement, pulp capping, pulpotomy and follow-up (0.43–0.56). For dual-labelled teeth, at least one acceptable category was predicted in 78.2% (YOLOv11) and 70.7% (YOLO26) of cases. Both architectures learned radiograph-based management categories with similar performance, lowest for categories whose distinction depends on clinical information. The models are a methodological step from diagnostic towards treatment-oriented tasks, not a substitute for clinical decision-making.

title: The Performance of Artificial Intelligence Applications in the Diagnosis, Radiographic Localization, and Treatment Planning of Periapical Lesions Under Zero-Shot Conditions
abstract: Abstract Background The aim of this study is to comparatively evaluate the performance of three different artificial intelligence applications (Claude, ChatGPT and Kimi Chat) in the diagnosis of periapical lesions, radiographic localization and treatment planning in panoramic radiographs, tested under blind conditions, using the assessment of two endodontic specialists as the reference standard. Methods The study included 100 panoramic radiographs. Each radiograph was presented to the artificial intelligence applications alongside the relevant clinical scenario and using a standard prompt. The model responses were classified as correct or incorrect by comparing them with the reference standard in terms of diagnosis, radiographic marking and treatment planning. Accuracy rates were calculated as n (%) and 95% confidence intervals were determined using the Wilson method. The Cochran’s Q test was used for comparisons between models, whilst the Bonferroni-corrected McNemar exact test was used for pairwise comparisons. Agreement between models was assessed using Fleiss’ Kappa, whilst inter-rater and intra-rater agreement were assessed using Cohen’s Kappa coefficient. Results The correct diagnosis rates were 36% for ChatGPT, 20% for Kimi, and 15% for Claude (p = 0.002), with ChatGPT performing significantly better than Claude (p < 0.001). In radiographic localization, Claude achieved the highest accuracy (90%), followed by Kimi (70%) and ChatGPT (54%), with significant differences in all pairwise comparisons (p < 0.0167). Accuracy in treatment planning ranged from 95% to 100%, with no significant difference between the models (p = 0.082). Inter- and intra-rater agreement was perfect (κ = 1.00). Conclusion The findings indicate that off-the-shelf (general-purpose) AI applications are not suitable for use as a primary, independent diagnostic tool in the interpretation of endodontic radiographs. However, their success in tasks such as radiographic annotation and treatment planning suggests that these models could be used as decision-support tools under specialist supervision or as auxiliary tools in dental education.

title: DDSF-Net: A Dual-Domain Synergistic Fusion Network with Spatial-Frequency Interaction for Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Medical image segmentation remains challenging when blurred boundaries, heterogeneous textures,and cross-scale anatomical variation must be handled simultaneously. Although hybrid CNN-Transformer models improve global context modeling, their skip fusion and decoder reconstructionstages often treat spatial structure and frequency cues in a coupled and content-agnostic manner.To address this limitation, we propose DDSF-Net, a U-shaped segmentation network that com-bines dual-domain skip fusion with dynamic upsampling. A Dual-Domain Feature Extraction Module(DDFEM) contains a spatial structural path (SSP) and a frequency texture path (FTP), together with internal gating and fusion operations. Boundary-Residual Synergistic Skip (BRS-Skip) connec-tions apply DDFEM to encoder and decoder features, then integrate a boundary-feature branch and encoder-residual mixing. In the decoder, a Dynamic Spatial-adaptive Upsampler (DSAU) performs content-aware offset sampling to better preserve boundary details during resolution recovery. Exper-iments on the Synapse, ACDC, and ISIC datasets show that DDSF-Net consistently improves theCSWin-UNet baseline and achieves competitive performance across different imaging modalities. On Synapse, DDSF-Net reaches 82.37% Dice and 17.91 mm HD95. Ablation studies further indicate that the combination of dual-domain skip fusion and dynamic upsampling contributes to the final gains.

title: Dynamic MRI-measured extension-position dorsal CSF space and long-term neurological outcomes after posterior cervical decompression for cervical spondylotic myelopathy: A retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Objective To examine whether hyperextension position dCSF predicts 12‑month neurological recovery after CSM posterior decompression and assess the prognostic value of postoperative occult positional cord compression. Methods This retrospective single-center cohort included 109 CSM patients receiving posterior cervical decompression. postoperative 3-month neutral and hyperextension dynamic MRI and 12-month clinical follow-up were performed, with dCSF measured at the target level. The primary outcome was mJOA recovery rate; secondary outcomes were NDI and subjective improvement. To eliminate confounding from static compression, analyses focused on the subgroup with neutral dCSF > 2 mm (n = 94), stratified into occult compression (hyperextension dCSF < 1 mm) and non-occult compression groups. Multivariable linear regression was used to identify independent predictors, and sensitivity analysis using absolute mJOA change confirmed the robustness. Results Extension dCSF (1.36 ± 0.47 mm) was significantly lower than neutral dCSF (2.71 ± 0.58 mm, P < 0.001). Extension dCSF correlated more strongly with the 12-month mJOA recovery rate; extension dCSF and preoperative disease duration were identified as independent predictors. The occult compression group (n = 17) exhibited poorer mJOA improvement (P < 0.01), with comparable NDI scores. Patients with occult compression had a longer preoperative disease duration. Sensitivity analysis confirmed stable findings. Conclusion Substantial dorsal CSF space loss may occur during neck extension even when satisfactory neutral-position decompression is achieved. Extension dCSF outperforms neutral dCSF for predicting neurological prognosis. Occult dynamic positional compression impairs long-term neurological recovery, which supports the clinical value of dynamic MRI for assessing the functional reserve of the spinal canal.

title: Stop-Gradient Gating for Deformable Image Registration: Monotonicity and Capacity-Constrained Collapse
abstract: Abstract Most deformable image registration models enforce uniform smoothness, spreading deformation capacity evenly across the image. This assumption becomes a bottleneck for medical images with heterogeneous displacement demands. It leads to over-deformation in structurally stable regions and under-deformation in high-motion areas. To address this limitation, we introduce a gated image registration framework that spatially modulates deformation capacity using a learned multiplicative gate. In practice, the gate allocates deformation capacity across regions to achieve optimal alignment. A stop-gradient operator decouples the gat-ing branch from the registration objective. This defines three training regimes, including none, partial, and full. In the partial regime, the stop-gradient blocks gradients of the registration objective, and only sparsity regularization influences the gating parameters. As a result, the mean gate activation drops from ≈ 0.29 to 0.0033, and registration collapses (NCC falls from 0.985 to 0.809) once deformation demand exceeds the model’s effective representational capacity. We characterize this collapse behavior, showing monotonic decay and a sharp transition determined by a critical gate threshold g †. Controlled synthetic experiments and three medical imaging datasets confirm the collapse, which remains absent in low-deformation settings. We further show that this instability can be mitigated by increasing the learning-rate ratio of the gate to the deformation network or by introducing controlled gradient leakage with a target-aware sparsity objective. This insight provides a simple design principle for stable gated registration. Never leave sparsity alone without balancing it against a registration gradient or a high gate learning rate.

title: Clinical and Molecular Characteristics of Pediatric Congenital Anomalies of the Kidney and Urinary Tract in Northwest China: A Multicenter Prospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Background Congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) are a leading cause of chronic kidney disease (CKD) in children, yet regional clinical and molecular data from Northwest China remain limited. This study characterized the clinical presentation and molecular etiology of CAKUT in a pediatric multicenter cohort, and evaluated the diagnostic utility of integrated trio whole-exome sequencing (WES) and genome-wide copy number variation sequencing (CNV-Seq). Methods In this prospective multicenter study, 91 consecutive children with CAKUT (aged 0–14 years) were enrolled at three tertiary centers between January 2022 and December 2024. Phenotyping included kidney ultrasound graded by the Society for Fetal Urology (SFU) and Urinary Tract Dilation (UTD) systems. Molecular analysis used trio-based WES and CNV-Seq. Variants were classified per ACMG/AMP 2015 guidelines. Results The male-to-female ratio was 3.3:1. Diagnosis was made within the first year of life in 44.0%, and 46.2% of cases were detected prenatally. Hydronephrosis was the most prevalent subtype (74.7%). Among patients with sufficient follow-up, CKD was present in 90.1%, and urinary tract infections occurred in 41.8%. Combined WES and CNV-Seq yielded a molecular diagnosis in 13.2% of patients: single-nucleotide variants or indels were identified by WES in 7.7%, and clinically significant copy number variants by CNV-Seq in 5.5%. Molecular diagnosis directly altered clinical management in several cases, including reclassification of imaging-based hydronephrosis and initiation of extra-kidney surveillance. Conclusion s In this cohort of children with CAKUT from Northwest China, integrated WES and CNV-Seq established an etiologic diagnosis in 13.2% of patients and informed clinical management. These findings support incorporation of advanced genetic testing into the diagnostic workflow for pediatric CAKUT to refine prognostication and personalized care.

title: Incidental Detection of Previously Unknown Chronic Infarcts on Outpatient Neuroimaging: A Target for Opportunistic Screening
abstract: Abstract Purpose Chronic infarcts on neuroimaging may represent previously unrecognized stroke and are an opportunity to initiate or escalate secondary prevention. The purpose of the study is to determine the prevalence of previously unknown chronic infarcts on outpatient neuroimaging and identify associated factors. Methods This retrospective, cross-sectional study evaluated adult outpatient imaging encounters including portions of the brain between October 1 and December 31, 2025. A database search for terms related to encephalomalacia was used to identify encounters. Medical record review determined if chronic infarcts were previously unknown or known, and infarcts were measured and localized. Univariate and multivariate regression analyses were performed to identify characteristics associated with unknown infarcts. Result Of 13,668 relevant neuroimaging encounters, 446 encounters from 419 unique patients demonstrated chronic infarcts, 45.6% (n = 191) of which were previously unknown. Univariate analysis associated previously unknown infarcts with MRI modality (OR: 2.26, 95% CI: 1.49–3.44, p < 0.001), and brainstem (OR: 5.59, 95% CI: 1.19–26.18, p = 0.03), gangliocapsular (OR: 2.33, 95% CI: 1.43–3.78, p < 0.001), or cerebellar location (OR: 2.29, 95% CI: 1.40–3.74, p < 0.001). Multivariate analysis identified small infarct size (OR: 2.44, 95% CI: 1.85–3.33, p < 0.001) as an independent predictor of previously unknown infarcts. Conclusion 45.6% of chronic infarcts identified on outpatient neuroimaging were previously unknown. Smaller infarct size was independently associated with previously unknown stroke. Incidentally detection represents an opportunity to evaluate patients for stroke etiology and initiate secondary stroke prevention.

title: Low-Intensity Focused Ultrasound for Facial Volume Restoration: A Retrospective Case Series
abstract: Abstract Purpose: Loss of facial volume due to aging or lipoatrophy significantly impacts appearance and psychosocial well-being. This study reports preliminary clinical outcomes of a non-injectable alternative: low-intensity, linear-focused ultrasound for facial volume restoration. Patients and methods: This retrospective case series included three female patients (aged 39, 43, and 52 years) with temporal or malar hollowing who declined injectables. All were treated in 2024 at a single aesthetic center using the LinearZ device (Jeisys Medical Inc., South Korea). Treatment was individualized by region (0.2–0.4 J, 20–100 shots, 4.5 mm cartridges). Standardized photographs were obtained at baseline and follow-up (3 months for all patients, and up to 6 months for one). A board-certified dermatologist blinded to the procedure assessed outcomes by comparing photographs and patient feedback. Results: Patient 1 (39 years) showed sustained improvement in bilateral temporal volume and contour at 3 and 6 months. Patient 2 (52 years) demonstrated increased left cheek volume with improved symmetry at 3 months. Patient 3 (43 years) exhibited enhanced midface volume, mandibular contour, and reduced laxity following dual-region treatment at 3 months. No adverse events or safety concerns were reported across patients. Improvements appeared gradually, consistent with remodeling processes rather than immediate filling. Conclusion: A single session of low-intensity, linear-focused ultrasound was associated with visible improvement in temporal and malar volume, as well as mandibular contour, without adverse events. These findings support the potential of subablative ultrasound as a safer, non-injectable alternative for mild to moderate facial volume loss. However, the small sample size, lack of volumetric measurements, and short follow-up limit generalizability. Controlled trials with objective endpoints and long-term evaluation are warranted.

title: Sharp but Wrong? Fidelity and Hallucination in Deep CT Super-Resolution with Analytic Phantoms
abstract: Abstract Deep super-resolution (SR) techniques could potentially recover the resolution that X-ray computed tomography (CT) sacrifices to reduce radiation dose and scanning time. However, in CT imaging, generating details that appear plausible but are not physically present represents a critical failure that standard evaluation metrics cannot detect.In this study, we train two deep-learning models to upsample CT slices: a pixel-loss residual network (EDSR) and an adversarially trained network (ESRGAN). Both models are evaluated in terms of reconstruction fidelity and their tendency to hallucinate image details.To assess hallucinated details, we use analytical phantoms containing line-pair gratings and pores with precisely known frequencies and diameters. The evaluation includes held-out frequency bands, a documented blur–decimation–noise model, and a validated spectral measurement method that classifies each grating as resolved, washed out, aliased, or hallucinated.At ×4 upscaling, all neural networks improve PSNR by more than 6 dB compared with bicubic and Lanczos interpolation. ESRGAN achieves the best perceptual score (LPIPS = 0.015 compared with 0.046 for EDSR), at the cost of approximately 2 dB in reconstruction fidelity. However, ESRGAN hallucinates 61% of the gratings that cannot be represented in the input image, whereas interpolation methods produce no hallucinated gratings.An adversarial-weight sweep demonstrates that perceptual loss alone is responsible for these invented details. Pixel-loss networks also exhibit limitations, replacing held-out gratings just below the Nyquist limit with their aliased counterparts learned during training.At ×2 upscaling, hallucination rates decrease substantially but do not disappear entirely, with ESRGAN still hallucinating 27% of the gratings. Interestingly, pores and thin lines that were never encountered during training are successfully recovered by all networks.All experimental data are synthetic and reproducible using a specified random seed.

title: Segmentation-Free Estimation of Fibre, Matrix and Void Fractions from Simulated X-ray CT of Fibre Composites with a 3D Residual Network
abstract: Abstract Fibre volume fraction and void content govern the stiffness and interlaminar strength of fibre-reinforced polymers, but measuring them from X-ray computed tomography (CT) normally requires voxel-wise segmentation, which is fragile when carbon fibre and epoxy differ little in attenuation and when fibres are only a few voxels across. We instead regress the three volume fractions of a CT sub-volume directly using a 3D residual network (3.6 million parameters, with a softmax output ensuring that the fractions sum to one). Training and test data are simulated: 66 synthetic composites with fibre contents ranging from 40% to 66% and void contents ranging from 0% to 5% are generated on a supersampled grid, ensuring that every crop has exact ground truth. The composites are scanned using a physics-based CT simulator incorporating parallel-beam projection, Poisson noise at three dose levels, detector blur, and filtered back-projection. On 216 test crops from 9 held-out composites, the network achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.84 percentage points (pp) [95% confidence interval: 0.66–1.05] for fibre and 0.17 pp [0.11–0.25] for void, compared with 6.06 pp and 0.28 pp, respectively, for the best threshold- or histogram-based methods. The network is more accurate on all 9 test composites for fibre and matrix (Wilcoxon p = 0.0039, the minimum attainable value for n = 9). Its fibre error increases only from 0.69 to 1.07 pp as the contrast-to-noise ratio decreases from 5.2 to 1.2. For void estimation, the network does not significantly outperform a Gaussian-mixture histogram fit (p = 0.36) and tends to overestimate void content below 1%. A mean-grey-value estimator calibrated on validation data achieves comparable performance (1.09 vs 0.87 pp; p = 0.20). However, a 2% calibration error increases its estimation error to 8.4 pp, whereas the network, whose input is normalized independently for each crop, remains completely unaffected.

title: Connected vs. Isolated Pore Classification via Learned Refinement of Connected-Component Analysis
abstract: Abstract The classification of isolated versus interconnected pores in porous media is critical for structural and fatigue assessments, yet classical 26-connectivity connected-component (CC) labeling fails catastrophically under realistic computed tomography (CT) noise due to the formation of false artifact webs. This study proposes a two-stage machine learning refinement pipeline to correct classical thresholding errors. Following Watershed over-segmentation to generate a proposal graph, we extract handcrafted geometric features—specifically minimum neck radius and path intensity—which successfully separate physical bridges from disconnected noise. We evaluate an XGBoost classifier, a GraphSAGE Graph Neural Network (GNN), and a 3D-CNN against the unrefined CC baseline. Feature importance analysis confirms that the tree-based model anchors its predictions on true physical geometry rather than random noise. While Watershed over-segmentation causes localized false-split penalties under the global Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), the learned refinement models achieve robust edge-level connectivity classification (Validation F1 ≥ 0.94), successfully severing the noise-induced bridge artifacts that compromise classical 26-connectivity thresholding.

title: When Near-Perfect Accuracy Is a Warning Sign: Frame-Level Data Leakage in 3D CNN Classification of the Alzheimer's Disease Spectrum from fMRI Volumes
abstract: Abstract Deep learning studies on neuroimaging data frequently report accuracies close to 100%, yet such results can arise from data leakage rather than from learned disease signal. This paper is a case study of that failure in the author’s own work. A 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) was trained to separate Alzheimer’s disease (AD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), early MCI (EMCI) and cognitively normal (CN) participants using 191,428 individual 3D volumes extracted from functional MRI (fMRI) acquisitions in the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). Each time frame was treated as an independent image, and the pooled frames were split at random, at the image level, into training and validation sets. The network reached 100% validation accuracy by epoch 14 and made no errors on any of the 191,428 volumes. We show that this outcome is explained by frame-level leakage: frames of the same participant are nearly identical, so a model can recognise individuals instead of disease stages, and a random split places almost every participant on both sides. We document the training signatures that exposed the problem, relate them to leakage patterns reported in the Alzheimer’s literature, quantify why image-level splitting of fMRI frames guarantees subject overlap, and propose a subject-level evaluation protocol. The corrected experiment is left to future work; the contribution of this paper is a transparent, reproducible account of how a plausible pipeline yields an invalid result, and how to detect it.

We show that this outcome is explained by frame-level leakage: frames of the same participant are nearly identical, so a model can recognise individuals instead of disease stages, and a random split places almost every participant on both sides. We document the training signatures that exposed the problem, relate them to leakage patterns reported in the Alzheimer’s literature, quantify why image-level splitting of fMRI frames guarantees subject overlap, and propose a subject-level evaluation protocol. The corrected experiment is left to future work; the contribution of this paper is a transparent, reproducible account of how a plausible pipeline yields an invalid result, and how to detect it.

title: Women Reach the Advanced Colorectal Neoplasia Risk of Men 17 Years Later: A Cross-Sectional Study of 9,795 Colonoscopies
abstract: Abstract Background The male excess of colorectal neoplasia is well established, but has not been expressed as the age at which women reach the same absolute risk, the quantity relevant to when screening should begin. Aims To estimate this risk-equivalent age offset, locate where in the sequence the disparity arises, and test whether it is segment-specific. Methods We retrospectively analysed 9,795 consecutive single-centre colonoscopies performed between January 2020 and October 2025. Outcomes were extracted from free-text endoscopy and pathology reports by a rule-based natural language processing algorithm with organ-specific attribution. The primary outcome was advanced neoplasia (advanced adenoma or colorectal cancer). Odds ratios came from logistic regression adjusted for age and year with patient-clustered standard errors, refitted in five pre-specified subsets. Sex-specific risk curves were fitted and their horizontal distance measured at matched risk. Results Women reached the risk of 55-year-old men 16.8 years later (95% confidence interval 12.8 to 22.7), an offset stable across screening thresholds. Advanced neoplasia occurred in 10.7% of men and 5.4% of women (adjusted odds ratio 1.98, 1.70 to 2.32), and the excess was similar at every earlier stage, from 1.73 for cancer to 2.02 for advanced adenoma (p < 0.001). It did not interact with age (p = 0.680) and persisted proximally (2.19), distally (1.98) and in every subset. Conclusions On the age axis, women reach the risk of men about 17 years later. The disparity is present from the earliest precursor lesion and constant thereafter, raising the hypothesis that a risk-equivalent screening threshold is crossed earlier in men.
