title: Position-associated intraluminal flow disturbance in idealized straight anal fistula tracts under sphincter loading: a clinically motivated proof-of-concept fluid-structure interaction study.
abstract: Background Anal fistula management remains clinically challenging because durable eradication of fistulous sepsis must be balanced against preservation of sphincter function. Although current surgical concepts emphasize fistula anatomy, internal-opening management, and drainage of septic tracts, the potential contribution of sphincter-induced biomechanical loading to intraluminal flow organization remains insufficiently explored. This clinically motivated proof-of-concept study investigated whether tract position within the sphincter complex is associated with different flow-disturbance patterns under controlled idealized conditions. Methods A female anal sphincter complex was reconstructed from pelvic MRI using Mimics and 3-Matic. Two idealized straight cylindrical synthetic fistula tracts with an identical diameter of 3 mm were embedded at anterior and lateral positions within the same anatomical model. Bidirectional fluid-structure interaction (FSI) simulations were performed using ANSYS Workbench. Standardized pseudocolor velocity maps from 0.01 to 0.06 s were processed using lumen region-of-interest ROI definition, color-to-velocity mapping, normalized velocity-index calculation, low-velocity segmentation, connected-component analysis, axial segmentation, and temporal reorganization analysis. Results Both configurations showed very low Reynolds numbers, consistent with viscosity-dominated laminar flow. Compared with the lateral tract, the anterior tract showed a lower mean velocity index 0.431 vs. 0.547, lower image-derived mean velocity 3.08 × 10 -3 vs. 3.91 × 10 -3 m/s, and higher low-velocity fraction 0.613 vs. 0.419 using the primary threshold of 0.4× vmax . The anterior tract also showed a larger normalized maximum connected low-velocity area 0.593 vs. 0.328 and a more broadly distributed axial low-velocity burden. The anterior configuration demonstrated earlier and more sustained low-velocity organization, whereas the lateral configuration showed relatively preserved early flow followed by greater late-phase expansion and temporal reorganization. Conclusion In this idealized single-anatomy model, tract position was associated with distinct intraluminal flow-disturbance descriptors under sphincter loading. These findings do not establish a clinical mechanism of recurrence or predict failure of sphincter-preserving procedures. Rather, they provide preliminary biomechanical evidence supporting future patient-specific studies that incorporate realistic tract geometries, male and female anatomies, posterior configurations, biological variability, and clinical validation.

title: Ultrasound-responsive microbubble platforms in lung cancer: mechanisms, molecular targeting, and therapeutic applications.
abstract: Lung cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, while the heterogeneous tumor microenvironment, abnormal vasculature, elevated interstitial fluid pressure, hypoxia, and dense extracellular matrix substantially limit the efficacy of conventional systemic therapies. Ultrasound-responsive microbubbles (MBs) have emerged as versatile theranostic platforms capable of overcoming several of these delivery barriers through externally controlled acoustic cavitation. This review comprehensively discusses the evolution, physicochemical characteristics, composition, and functional mechanisms of MB-based systems for lung cancer diagnosis and therapy. Particular emphasis is placed on stable and inertial cavitation, sonoporation, microstreaming, vascular permeabilization, and enhanced transport of therapeutic agents into tumor tissue. The diagnostic potential of targeted MBs for contrast-enhanced ultrasound, molecular imaging, perfusion assessment, and super-resolution visualization of tumor vasculature is highlighted. Therapeutic applications encompassing chemotherapeutics, nucleic acids, microRNAs, oxygen delivery, immunotherapy, and combination strategies with radiotherapy are critically examined. The review also discusses molecularly targeted MBs, nanoparticle-MB hybrids, and ultrasound-triggered modulation of the tumor immune microenvironment. Despite promising preclinical outcomes, challenges involving pulmonary acoustic attenuation, short circulation time, biodistribution, treatment parameter standardization, manufacturing, safety, and regulatory requirements remain. Emerging theranostic, hybrid, and artificial intelligence-assisted platforms may facilitate personalized and clinically translatable microbubble-based precision therapy for lung cancer.

title: Case Report: Diagnosis and treatment analysis of a case of primary pulmonary sarcoma.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to explore the clinical features, diagnostic points, and treatment strategies of primary pulmonary artery sarcoma (PPAS) and improve the understanding of this rare disease. Methods A retrospective analysis of the clinical data of a PPAS patient admitted to our hospital in December 2021 was conducted. The clinical manifestations, imaging features, pathological diagnosis, and treatment process were systematically summarized, followed by a discussion based on the literature. Results The patient was a 39-year-old female who presented with dry cough and fatigue, and gradually developed hemoptysis, chest pain, and difficulty breathing. Multimodal imaging examination revealed a mass in the upper lobe of the left lung with extensive pulmonary embolism, and PET/CT suggested increased glucose metabolism at the site of pulmonary embolism. The postoperative pathological diagnosis was polymorphic undifferentiated sarcoma, and immunohistochemistry exhibited high expression of Ki-67 (60%). Genetic testing revealed TP53 mutations and increased CDK4 copy number. The patient underwent surgical resection combined with targeted therapy and radiotherapy. Follow-up indicated tumor reduction, symptom relief, and survival exceeding 14 months. Conclusion The clinical manifestations of PPAS lack specificity and are easily misdiagnosed as pulmonary thromboembolism. Multimodal imaging evaluation, timely histopathological examination, and individualized comprehensive treatment are crucial for improving prognosis.

title: Hybrid near-infrared spectroscopy-intravascular ultrasound imaging: integrating plaque biology, procedural precision, and prognostic stratification in contemporary coronary intervention.
abstract: Hybrid near-infrared spectroscopy-intravascular ultrasound (NIRS/IVUS) represents a major advancement in intracoronary imaging as it combines an ultra-high-resolution ultrasound image processing of the vessel lumen and atherosclerotic plaque with an automated algorithm for the detection and quantification of the plaque lipid-core. This unique feature allows for a detailed biologic assessment of the plaque composition and quantification beyond the conventional angiographic estimation of coronary artery stenosis severity. High lipidic atherosclerotic burden, as this is predominantly defined by maxLCBI 4mm ≥400, identifies high-risk vulnerable plaques and independently predicts future non-culprit major cardiovascular events and a higher risk of periprocedural myocardial injury during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Segments with maxLCBI 4mm >400 carry a 3- to 4-fold higher risk of non-culprit events (LRP), and lesions combining plaque burden ≥70% with maxLCBI 4mm ≥324.7 have a 7% 4-year event rate (PROSPECT II). Emerging evidence from the PREVENT trial suggests that preventive PCI of imaging-defined vulnerable plaques may reduce future events, although this benefit was driven predominantly by ischaemia-driven revascularization and hospitalization rather than by reductions in death or myocardial infarction. This strategy therefore remains investigational, and it is not yet incorporated into major guideline recommendations. NIRS-IVUS has additionally been used to demonstrate the prognostic value of lipid reduction after successful PCI. In this review, we provide a mechanistic synthesis of key randomized trials (PROSPECT II, LRP, and PREVENT) and observational registries to summarize contemporary evidence for the use of NIRS/IVUS in cardiovascular risk stratification, vulnerable-plaque detection, and PCI optimization, including the potential prognostic implications of post-PCI residual lipid burden. We also present case examples and a proposed, investigational algorithm for integrating the NIRS/IVUS system into lesion-level clinical decision-making.

Segments with maxLCBI<sub>4mm</sub> >400 carry a 3- to 4-fold higher risk of non-culprit events (LRP), and lesions combining plaque burden ≥70% with maxLCBI<sub>4mm</sub> ≥324.7 have a 7% 4-year event rate (PROSPECT II). Emerging evidence from the PREVENT trial suggests that preventive PCI of imaging-defined vulnerable plaques may reduce future events, although this benefit was driven predominantly by ischaemia-driven revascularization and hospitalization rather than by reductions in death or myocardial infarction. This strategy therefore remains investigational, and it is not yet incorporated into major guideline recommendations. NIRS-IVUS has additionally been used to demonstrate the prognostic value of lipid reduction after successful PCI. In this review, we provide a mechanistic synthesis of key randomized trials (PROSPECT II, LRP, and PREVENT) and observational registries to summarize contemporary evidence for the use of NIRS/IVUS in cardiovascular risk stratification, vulnerable-plaque detection, and PCI optimization, including the potential prognostic implications of post-PCI residual lipid burden. We also present case examples and a proposed, investigational algorithm for integrating the NIRS/IVUS system into lesion-level clinical decision-making.

title: Prognostic value of model for end-stage liver disease excluding international normalized ratio score combined with late gadolinium enhancement in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
abstract: Introduction Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) is one of the main subtypes of heart failure (HF). Model for end-stage liver disease excluding international normalized ratio (MELD-XI) score and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) each independently predict adverse prognosis in HF patients. Methods This retrospective study enrolled adult HFrEF patients admitted to Qilu Hospital of Shandong University between September 2018 and January 2023. The primary endpoint was defined as a composite endpoint of rehospitalization for HF and all-cause mortality. Multivariate Cox regression model was established to evaluate the effects of LGE and MELD-XI score on the primary endpoint. We also evaluate the incremental prognostic value of adding the MELD-XI score to the model. Results A total of 246 HFrEF patients were included and 55 patients reached the primary endpoint during follow-up. In the adjusted Cox regression model, for each standard deviation increase in LGE and MELD-XI score, the hazard ratios (HRs) for primary endpoint were 1.52 (95% CI: 1.23-1.88) and 1.60 (95% CI: 1.31-1.94), respectively. Adding MELD-XI score into model improved its incremental prognostic performance [ Δ C-Statistic: 0.052 (95% CI: 0.001-0.092), p = 0.039; Continuous NRI: 0.399 (95% CI: 0.077-0.532), p = 0.027; IDI: 0.094 (95% CI: 0.018-0.174), p = 0.010]. Conclusions Both CMR-assessed LGE and MELD-XI score were associated with adverse outcomes in patients with HFrEF. Combining these two indicators provided complementary prognostic information for HFrEF patients.

title: Discordant low-gradient aortic stenosis: a phenotype-first, likelihood-tiered multimodality imaging framework.
abstract: Discordant low-gradient aortic stenosis (AS), commonly defined by the aortic valve area (AVA) ≤1.0 cm 2 with mean gradient <40 mmHg and peak velocity <4.0 m/s, is reported in up to 40% of patients evaluated for AS in selected cohorts. Current guidelines and consensus documents outline echocardiographic quality control, haemodynamic phenotype assignment, dobutamine stress echocardiography (DSE), CT aortic valve calcium scoring (CT-AVC), and integrated assessment, yet uncertainty persists when haemodynamic, structural, symptomatic, and myocardial findings diverge. This narrative review proposes a phenotype-first, likelihood-tiered multimodality framework that adds four operational elements to current guidance: routine documentation of transvalvular flow rate, phenotype-specific interpretation of DSE and CT-AVC, separation of valve severity adjudication from myocardial risk refinement, and structured reporting of residual uncertainty. DSE with projected AVA is favoured for flow-dependent severity assessment in classical low-flow low-gradient AS, whereas CT-AVC likelihood categories are emphasised in preserved-ejection-fraction low-gradient phenotypes and after inconclusive DSE. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance, global longitudinal strain, extracellular volume fraction, and cardiac damage staging are used as prognostic and counselling adjuncts, not stand-alone triggers for valve intervention. Indeterminate cases are reported as unresolved discordance with the basis of uncertainty stated explicitly. The approach is intended to improve Heart Team communication and requires prospective validation before use as a treatment algorithm.

title: Cardiac CT in ANOCA, INOCA, and MINOCA: a structured narrative review of evidence, applications, and limitations.
abstract: Cardiac computed tomography (CT) depicts coronary anatomy and provides additional physiological and myocardial measurements in angina or ischemia with non-obstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA/INOCA) and acute non-obstructive presentations. This structured narrative review examines what these measurements establish about anatomy, vasomotor mechanisms, prognosis, and clinical utility. Six-domain searches of PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL, supplemented by citation-based sources and ClinicalTrials.gov, were updated through 23 September 2026. The bibliographic inventory contains 154 publications; selection was targeted, involving single-assessor historical screening and revision-stage triage rather than a systematic-review process. Contemporary MINOCA denotes myocardial injury with non-obstructive coronary arteries as a working diagnosis; historical study definitions are preserved. Conventional coronary CT angiography depicts plaque, anomalies, myocardial bridging, and selected coronary-wall abnormalities. Plaque and pericoronary-fat associations vary with the population and reference standard. Small syndrome-specific studies and related cohorts provide limited diagnostic evidence; prognostic associations do not validate vasomotor endotyping. CT-derived fractional flow reserve concerns epicardial pressure loss, while CT perfusion does not independently identify a vasomotor mechanism. Late iodine enhancement and CT-derived extracellular volume provide myocardial information, but agreement with individual cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) measurements does not establish equivalence to multiparametric CMR. After non-obstructive invasive angiography, additional CT should answer a defined residual question and justify contrast exposure, radiation, and diagnostic delay. The evidence examined in this review does not establish that an advanced CT biomarker strategy improves mechanism-specific treatment selection or patient outcomes in ANOCA/INOCA or an acute MINOCA pathway.

title: Patient-level diagnostic performance of myocardial contrast echocardiography using ultrasound-enhancing agents after acute myocardial infarction: comparison with radionuclide perfusion-metabolism imaging.
abstract: Objective This study evaluated the patient-level diagnostic performance and agreement of myocardial contrast echocardiography (MCE) for assessing myocardial viability after acute myocardial infarction (AMI), using combined radionuclide perfusion-metabolism imaging as the reference standard. Methods This retrospective diagnostic-comparison study included 141 patients with AMI who underwent MCE and reference radionuclide perfusion-metabolism imaging between February 2017 and February 2023. Imaging was generally performed during the subacute phase, 7-14 days after symptom onset. Reference assessment combined 99 mTc-MIBI myocardial perfusion imaging with 18 F-FDG metabolic imaging. The standardized 17-segment left ventricular model was used as an anatomical framework for image interpretation; however, because individual segment-level classifications were not systematically archived, diagnostic performance was evaluated at the patient level. MCE examinations were interpreted independently by experienced cardiologists blinded to the reference imaging results, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), and Cohen's kappa were calculated with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Reference imaging classified 91 patients as having viable myocardium and 50 as having non-viable myocardium. MCE yielded 79 true-positive, 44 true-negative, 6 false-positive, and 12 false-negative classifications. Patient-level sensitivity was 86.81% (95% CI, 78.35%-92.29%), specificity was 88.00% (95% CI, 76.20%-94.38%), and overall accuracy was 87.23% (95% CI, 80.72%-91.77%). PPV was 92.94% (95% CI, 85.44%-96.72%), and NPV was 78.57% (95% CI, 66.18%-87.29%). Agreement between MCE and reference imaging was substantial (Cohen's κ = 0.728; 95% CI, 0.612-0.845; P < 0.001). Conclusion MCE demonstrated substantial patient-level agreement with radionuclide perfusion-metabolism imaging for post-AMI myocardial viability assessment. These findings support its potential role as a complementary diagnostic imaging modality under the evaluated conditions. However, the present study did not assess subsequent functional recovery, ventricular remodeling, revascularization benefit, treatment decisions, or clinical outcomes; therefore, no conclusions regarding patient-management benefit or prognostic utility can be drawn from these data.

title: SynForge-Cardio: a unified multimodal synthetic dataset generation framework for privacy-preserving cardiovascular AI.
abstract: Multimodal cardiovascular AI systems benefit from jointly available chest radiographs, 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs), and structured electronic health record (EHR) variables. In practice, multi-institutional model development is constrained by privacy regulations, institutional data silos, and class imbalance for less common findings. Existing open-source synthetic data tools are largely modality-specific: tabular libraries such as Synthetic Data Vault (SDV)/Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN), image generators based on latent diffusion, and time-series methods such as Time-series Generative Adversarial Network (TimeGAN) each require its own setup, configuration, and validation. This study presents SynForge-Cardio, a multimodality orchestration framework for prompt-driven synthetic dataset generation across chest X-ray (CXR), 12-lead ECG, and EHR modalities. Rather than introducing a new generative backbone, SynForge-Cardio coordinates established components-latent diffusion with optional low-rank adaptation for CXR; parametric and bounded morphology-preserving augmentation (with an optional TimeGAN path) for ECG; and size-aware routing among jitter augmentation, Gaussian copula, and CTGAN/Tabular Variational Autoencoder for EHR-behind a shared clinical prompt interface, a rule-based router, and a postgeneration quality/privacy reporting layer. The three modalities were generated independently from separate datasets; the framework does not perform patient-level joint synthesis and makes no claim of anatomical or physiological consistency across modalities. This system is implemented as a FastAPI backend with a React frontend and can run on a single workstation GPU. Herein, we formalize the orchestration objective, specify modality-wise models and metrics [Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), dynamic time warping (DTW), power spectral density similarity, Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistics, correlation preservation, and distance-to-closest-record privacy screening], and describe an evaluation protocol on public corpora (NIH Chest X-ray14, PTB-XL, and the UCI Cleveland Heart Disease dataset), including a four-regime train-on-synthetic/test-on-real (TSTR) utility analysis with five random seeds. On the framework alone, we measured 94.6% modality-routing accuracy, 100% direct-vs.-routed generation equivalence on the evaluated cases, 59 unnecessary generator calls avoided, and 100% validation/reporting completeness (1,105/1,108 tests pass, 3 skipped). Downstream-utility results were mixed: augmenting a 25%-real training set with synthetic data changed the held-out AUROC by -0.041 to +0.050 across three CXR tasks (none significant at five seeds); by +0.019 for ECG MI-vs.-NORM [produced by mode B (bounded real-waveform augmentation, whose synthetic samples can be matched to their true source recording at top-1 ≈ 42.7-43.4%, and hence, mode B is not an independently learned generative model)]; and by +0.017 for EHR heart disease classification, which is not evidence of benefit given the 61-record hold-out set (the test-set bootstrap 95% CI for the difference includes zero). Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV acquisition was not completed because credentialed access was unavailable; all reported EHR results were UCI-based. SynForge-Cardio is intended as a practical, reproducible research framework for privacy-conscious cardiovascular data augmentation and prototype development.

title: Case Report: Balancing atypical femoral fracture healing and bone metastasis control.
abstract: Background Bone-modifying agents (BMAs) represent standard supportive therapy for patients with bone metastases to mitigate skeletal-related events (SREs). Alongside improved cancer survival, cumulative antiresorptive exposure renders atypical femoral fracture (AFF) an important yet infrequent complication. For patients with active metastatic disease, clinical management poses unique challenges, since discontinuation of antiresorptive agents may elevate skeletal-related risk while sustained suppression may impede fracture healing. Case presentation A 56-year-old postmenopausal woman with metastatic breast cancer had received zoledronic acid (4 mg intravenously every 3 months) for 4 years. Because of progression of bone metastases and chest/back pain, treatment was changed to denosumab (120 mg monthly). After three doses, she developed bilateral thigh pain after a minor torsion injury, and radiographs demonstrated bilateral transverse femoral shaft fractures with lateral cortical thickening. Bilateral antegrade intramedullary nailing was performed. Intraoperative bone marrow pathology showed no tumor infiltration. Denosumab was discontinued. Two months later, because of persistent severe osteoporosis and increased bone resorption (β-CTX 0.65 ng/mL), zoledronic acid 4 mg every 12 weeks was restarted. Outcome Eight months after fixation, both fractures achieved radiographic healing with callus formation; no new skeletal-related events were documented during follow-up. Serum β-CTX decreased to 0.35 ng/mL. This clinical course suggests that de-escalated zoledronic acid therapy was temporally associated with fracture healing while sustaining continuous antiresorptive effects in this individual patient. Conclusion This case underscores the diagnostic necessity of distinguishing AFF from metastatic pathological fracture, as well as the therapeutic trade-off between fracture healing and sustained skeletal protection. Sequential antiresorptive exposure, notably prolonged bisphosphonate administration followed by denosumab, warrants vigilant clinical screening for potential AFF. Post-denosumab therapeutic strategies should take rebound bone turnover into consideration. The proposed risk-stratified surveillance framework is evidence-informed but remains unvalidated and should not be interpreted as formal clinical guidance.

title: Application of artificial intelligence in the diagnosis and treatment of thyroid cancer.
abstract: Thyroid cancer is one of the most common endocrine malignancies, and its rising incidence has increased the demand for more accurate and efficient diagnostic and management strategies. Current clinical management mainly relies on ultrasonography, fine-needle aspiration (FNA), surgery, radioactive iodine therapy, thyroid-stimulating hormone suppression, and systemic treatment in selected advanced cases. However, substantial interobserver variability, indeterminate cytology, and heterogeneity in tumor behavior still complicate diagnosis and risk stratification. In thyroid cancer, AI(Artificial intelligence) -assisted models have been applied to ultrasound, CT, MRI, cytology, histopathology, and genomic data, with promising performance in distinguishing benign from malignant nodules, predicting lymph node metastasis and key mutations, and supporting individualized management. This review critically synthesizes evidence across these applications, focusing on study design, validation strategies, generalizability, and clinical relevance. It also examines explainable AI, emerging foundation models, and regulatory and implementation challenges. Although many models report high diagnostic or predictive performance, these results alone do not establish improvements in clinical decision-making or patient outcomes. Prospective clinical validation, cost-effectiveness assessment, and evaluation of integration into clinical workflows are needed to determine whether AI provides meaningful benefits over standard care.

title: Opportunistic application of machine learning for bone health stratification in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
abstract: Purpose The primary objective of this study was to compare the performance of various machine learning (ML) models in the opportunistic screening of abnormal bone mineral density (BMD) among type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients using routine non-contrast-enhanced chest CT. Materials and methods A total of 249 T2DM patients (age range, 40-97 years; mean ± standard deviation, 60.93 ± 11.49 years) who underwent chest CT with quantitative CT (QCT) analysis were retrospectively enrolled between January 2021 and June 2024. Patients were randomly split at a 7:3 ratio into a training set (n=175) and an internal test set (n=74). Semi-automatic segmentation of the L1 vertebral body was performed using 3D Slicer, and 2273 radiomic features were extracted via the Research Portal V1.1 workstation. Six radiomics-based ML models were constructed; their predictive performance and stability for distinguishing normal versus abnormal BMD were evaluated and compared. Results Among the T2DM patients included, the incidence of abnormal BMD was 40.56% (101/249). Fifteen radiomic features were selected using the minimum redundancy-maximum relevance (MRMR) algorithm and incorporated into six ML models (RF, SVMRadial, SVMLinear, NNet, xgbLinear and KNNs). In nested cross-validation, the SVMLinear model achieved the better predictive performance (accuracy: 0.906 ± 0.032; area under the curve [AUC]: 0.945 ± 0.028), followed by the NNet model (accuracy: 0.906 ± 0.031; AUC: 0.941 ± 0.029). In terms of stability, the SVMLinear model exhibited greater robustness against data perturbation (relative standard deviation [RSD] of mean accuracy: 3.54%; RSD of mean AUC: 3.04%). Conclusions The ML models enable opportunistic prediction of BMD status from chest CT in patients with T2DM. Specifically, the L1-vertebra radiomics-based SVMLinear model achieves a favorable balance of discrimination ability and stability, and may serve as a useful tool for opportunistic clinical screening for abnormal BMD in this patient population.

title: The full spectrum of thyroid late effects following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in pediatrics: insights from a large multicenter cohort.
abstract: Introduction Thyroid disorders are among the most prevalent late sequelae of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). While total body irradiation (TBI) is an established risk factor, the toxicity of alkylating agent-based conditioning regimens remains poorly characterized. The present study aimed to: i) quantify the cumulative incidence (CI) of thyroid late effects in a large multicenter pediatric cohort; ii) identify the independent risk determinants of HSCT-related thyroid disorders; iii) assess the specific detrimental role of chemo-only conditioning regimens; iv) characterize longitudinal thyroid volumetric trajectories following HSCT. Methods Multicenter retrospective observational study enrolling 637 pediatric HSCT survivors transplanted between 1999 and 2023 across three referral Centers. Conditioning regimens included: TBI (40%), busulfan (32%), treosulfan (18%), other (10%). Endocrine surveillance encompassed 6-12-monthly thyroid function tests and ultrasound assessment over a mean follow-up of 11.0 ± 6.4 years. Results The 20-year CI achieved 43.1% for thyroid function disorders (TFD) and 71.2% for nodules. Concerning the conditioning regimen, the 20-year CI of TFD was 54%, 35% and 21% for TBI, busulfan and treosulfan, respectively (p=0.026). The CI of TFD was statistically lower following treosulfan than busulfan (p=0.039). Compared to treosulfan, both TBI (HR 2.39, p=0.006) and busulfan (HR 1.77, p=0.08) conferred an increased risk of TFD on multivariate analysis. Concerning ultrasonographic findings, the 18-year CI of thyroid nodules following TBI overtly exceeded chemo-only regimens, while treosulfan and busulfan showed comparable longitudinal trendlines (p 0.82). The right lobe anteroposterior diameter (RLD) Z-score was used as an indirect indicator of thyroid volume. Longitudinal ultrasonographic assessment revealed significantly greater RLD Z-scores following treosulfan compared with busulfan (p=0.002) and TBI (p<0.001). Finally, age<10 years at HSCT (p=0.013), severe graft versus host disease (p=0.036), TBI (P = 0.05) and elevated BMI (p=0.04) were independent determinants of the need for hormonal replacement therapy. Conclusions Treosulfan-based conditioning is associated with the lowest cumulative functional thyroid morbidity and the most favorable longitudinal volumetric profile among myeloablative regimens, outperforming busulfan on both endpoints and a lesser degree of thyrocyte damage.

title: Integrated imaging, body composition, and systemic immune-inflammatory profiling for non-invasive prediction of HER2 status in endometrial cancer.
abstract: Objectives Preoperative evaluation of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) status in endometrial cancer (EC) is clinically important for molecular stratification and treatment planning. This study aimed to develop a non-invasive predictive model integrating functional MRI-derived tumor characteristics, CT-derived body composition, and systemic immune-inflammatory markers for identifying HER2-positive EC. Methods In this single-center retrospective study, 75 patients with pathologically confirmed EC (41 HER2-positive, 34 HER2-negative) who underwent preoperative 3.0 T magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), including amide proton transfer-weighted (APTw) imaging and intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) diffusion-weighted imaging, and chest CT between August 2019 and June 2026 were evaluated. Quantitative MRI parameters, including APT values, the slow apparent diffusion coefficient (D), fast apparent diffusion coefficient (D*), and perfusion fraction (f), and CT-derived body composition, including visceral adipose tissue (VAT), subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT), skeletal muscle (SM) and intramuscular adipose tissue (IMAT), were extracted. Systemic immune-inflammatory parameters including neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio (NLR), monocyte to lymphocyte ratio (MLR), platelet to lymphocyte ratio (PLR) and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) were calculated. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent risk factors and build predictive models, with diagnostic efficacy assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis and internal validation using 1000-resample bootstrap. Results The HER2 (+) group demonstrated significantly higher APT values (2.76% vs. 2.44%), D* values (3.23 × 10- 3 mm 2 /s vs. 1.88 × 10- 3 mm 2 /s), f values (0.22 vs. 0.19), SAT area (138.38 cm 2 vs. 112.73 cm 2 ), and MLR values (0.19 vs. 0.14) compared with the HER2 (-) group, whereas lower D values (0.59 × 10- 3 mm 2 /s vs. 0.67 × 10- 3 mm 2 /s) were observed in the HER2 (+) group. Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified APT (OR = 9.368, P = 0.011), f (OR = 8.303, P = 0.002), SAT (OR = 1.017, P = 0.033), and MLR (OR = 8.336, P = 0.006) as independent predictors of HER2 positivity. The integrated model incorporating APT value, f, SAT, and MLR achieved an AUC of 0.879, sensitivity of 87.8%, and specificity of 79.4%. Conclusion An integrated model combining tumor imaging characteristics, body composition parameters, and systemic immune-inflammatory markers may provide a non-invasive approach for preoperative prediction of HER2-positive EC.

title: Neurovascular dysfunction in diabetic retinopathy: mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives.
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) involves dysfunction of the retinal neurovascular unit (NVU) in addition to clinically detectable microvascular lesions. This narrative review critically examines how metabolic and organelle stress, neuroglial inflammation, and blood-retinal barrier dysfunction contribute to impaired retinal homeostasis. We propose an evidence-to-decision framework that distinguishes candidate initiating mechanisms, disease amplifiers, persistence programs, and potential treatment-escape pathways according to the strength of causal evidence and clinical relevance. Findings from human studies, experimental models, and clinical trials are evaluated separately to avoid conflating molecular associations with established mechanisms of disease progression. Particular attention is given to the distinction between clinical metabolic memory and experimentally demonstrated molecular persistence, as well as between alternative angiogenic signaling and clinically validated resistance to vascular endothelial growth factor inhibition. Emerging imaging, electrophysiological, and molecular biomarkers may help characterize neurovascular heterogeneity, but their prognostic and predictive value remains insufficiently established. We identify key experimental and clinical studies needed to validate mechanistic hypotheses, clarify their relationship to functional outcomes, and assess their therapeutic relevance. This synthesis provides a framework for prioritizing testable mechanisms while emphasizing that mechanism-guided patient stratification and treatment selection require prospective clinical validation.

title: Pituitary residual tumor detection: incremental value of multimodal assessment.
abstract: Introduction Postoperative residual tumor is associated with regrowth and recurrence in pituitary adenomas, making maximal safe resection an important therapeutic goal. We evaluated the incremental contribution of microscopy, endoscopic inspection, and 3.0-T intraoperative magnetic resonance imaging (iMRI) to residual tumor detection and assessment of the planned extent of resection. Methods In this retrospective single-center cohort study, 120 consecutive eligible patients undergoing transsphenoidal surgery for pituitary adenoma underwent sequential microsurgical resection, endoscopic inspection, and iMRI. Results Initial endoscopic inspection confirmed the planned extent of resection in 95/120 patients (79.2%) and indicated further resection in 25/120 (20.8%). After any indicated further resection, repeat endoscopic inspection confirmed planned extent of resection achievement before iMRI in all 120 patients. At iMRI, planned extent of resection was judged achieved in 85/120 patients (70.8%), whereas residual tumor was suspected in 35/120 (29.2%) before any iMRI-triggered resection. Among 95 patients considered complete at initial endoscopic inspection, iMRI identified suspected residual tumor in 21 (22.1%). Escalation beyond microscopy was more frequent in recurrent than primary adenomas (12/14, 85.7% vs 34/106, 32.1%; p < 0.001). Each doubling of preoperative tumor volume was associated with higher odds of iMRI-suspected residual tumor (OR 1.79, 95% CI 1.32-2.44; p < 0.001). Discussion Sequential endoscopic inspection and iMRI provided complementary information beyond microsurgical assessment. Additional assessment was more frequently required in recurrent adenomas, while increasing preoperative tumor volume was associated with iMRI-suspected residual tumor. These findings support prospective evaluation of risk-adapted multimodal intraoperative assessment.

title: Radiomics- based biomarkers for immunotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer: advances, challenges, and future perspectives in biological interpretation and clinical translation.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet treatment benefit remains heterogeneous and resistance is common. Genomic alterations, tumor microenvironment (TME) remodeling, and metabolic reprogramming across spatial and temporal scales that are incompletely captured by single-site tissue sampling. Radiomics extracts quantitative features from routine images and offers a framework for investigating macroscopic correlates of these processes. This narrative review critically examines computed tomography (CT) and fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/CT (¹ 8 F-FDG PET/CT) radiomics in relation to oncogenic alterations, immune and stromal phenotypes, programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression, tumor mutational burden, and metabolic-immune interactions in NSCLC. It should be highlighted that such observed statistical links only generate plausible biological hypotheses and do not constitute experimental proof of true mechanistic relationships. Rather than merely summarizing predictive model performance, we emphasize evidence boundaries and interpretive caveats for radiomic-TME associations. We further elaborate on key translational bottlenecks including limited reproducibility, technical standardization deficits, and retrospective-model overfitting. We discuss ongoing efforts toward cross-scale multi-omics integration, alongside the promises and inherent limitations of explainable artificial intelligence and federated learning for clinical translation. To move beyond purely predictive tools toward mechanism-aware decision-support systems, future radiomic research requires prospective multicenter validation, rigorous data harmonization, and combined analyses integrating spatial transcriptomics, digital pathology, and circulating biomarkers for precision immuno-oncology.

title: Neoadjuvant treatment is associated with fibrotic and transcriptional remodeling of tumor-draining lymph nodes in rectal cancer.
abstract: Background Neoadjuvant treatment is associated with reduced lymph-node yield in rectal cancer, but the accompanying changes in tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs) remain incompletely characterized. Methods We analyzed Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results data, a 178-patient institutional cohort, quantitative histopathology of 447 histologically negative TDLNs from 159 patients, and bulk RNA sequencing of 30 nodes from 24 patients. Institutional comparisons distinguished a radiotherapy-containing treatment pathway (RT) from management without preoperative radiotherapy (NRT); in the institutional clinical cohort, all 105 RT patients and 10 of 73 NRT patients received neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Pathology models accounted for patient clustering, and RNA counts were aggregated within patients. Results Recorded preoperative radiotherapy was associated with lower examined-node counts in Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER). In the institutional cohort, the expanded pretreatment-adjusted incidence-rate ratio was 0.83 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.67-1.02]; pretreatment-covariate overlap weighting yielded 0.80 (95% CI, 0.66-0.96). RT-group nodes were more fibrotic and smaller, with lower germinal-center and lymphoid-tissue area fractions. Patient-level RNA-seq identified 4,446 differentially expressed genes, with higher extracellular-matrix and angiogenic programs and lower antigen-receptor and B-cell-receptor signaling. Selected pathway directions were retained across sensitivity analyses. Computational deconvolution provided supportive estimates of relative cell composition. Conclusion A radiotherapy-containing neoadjuvant treatment pathway, including chemoradiotherapy in the institutional clinical, pathology, and RNA-seq cohorts, was associated with lower node yield and structural and transcriptional differences in TDLNs. These findings characterize the nodal structural and transcriptional phenotype associated with neoadjuvant treatment.

title: Combined CD8 and granzyme B PET/CT reveals divergent immune responses to radiotherapy plus PD-1 blockade.
abstract: Background Combined radiotherapy (RT) and PD-1 blockade can elicit durable antitumor immunity, yet responses remain heterogeneous and difficult to predict with conventional anatomical imaging. Noninvasive visualization of functional immune activity could provide mechanistic insights into treatment response. Here, we evaluated a dual-tracer PET imaging strategy targeting CD8 + T-cell localization and granzyme B (GZMB)-associated cytotoxic activity during radiotherapy plus PD-1 blockade. Methods Female BALB/c mice bearing CT26 colorectal or 4T1 breast tumors were divided into phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), PD-1 blockade, radiotherapy (RT), or combined PD-1 blockade plus RT groups. 89 Zr-DFO-anti-CD8 PET/CT characterized baseline immune phenotype and treatment-associated CD8+ cell localization, whereas serial 68 Ga-NOTA-granzyme B-targeted probe (GZP) PET/CT assessed early granzyme B-associated effector activity. Tumor uptake was quantified as percentage injected dose per cubic centimeter (%ID/cc), and imaging findings were related to tumor growth and immunohistochemical staining. Results In CT26 tumors, the combination group showed significantly increased 89 Zr-DFO-anti-CD8 uptake at 120 hours (10.09 ± 1.05%ID/cc versus 7.01 ± 0.60%ID/cc in PBS; p < 0.001) and increased 68 Ga-NOTA-GZP uptake on day 9 (0.64 ± 0.13%ID/cc; p < 0.05 versus PBS and RT and p < 0.01 versus PD-1 blockade). In 4T1 tumors, combination treatment showed increased 89 Zr-DFO-anti-CD8 uptake at 72 hours (5.88 ± 0.60%ID/cc; p < 0.05 versus PBS group), whereas mean GZP uptake was not significantly different from monotherapy groups. Importantly, animals classified as responders based on a pre-defined day-20 tumor-growth inhibition (TGI) threshold exhibited higher GZP uptake on days 6 and 9 compared with non-responders. Conclusion Dual-tracer PET provides complementary information on CD8 + T-cell localization and GZMB-associated cytotoxic activity. Notably, the model-dependent CD8 and GZP signals in 4T1 tumors suggest that T-cell recruitment may not necessarily reflect effective cytotoxic function, supporting the complementary value of functional imaging alongside localization-based approaches. The findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating and support further preclinical and prospective clinical investigation.

title: Differential LAG3 expression in intestinal tissue reveals a dual-pathology model of steroid-refractory acute graft-versus-host disease.
abstract: Introduction Acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) of the gastrointestinal tract remains a leading cause of non-relapse mortality following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation, and steroid-refractory intestinal aGVHD carries a particularly poor prognosis. CD8 + T cells are critical effectors of intestinal tissue injury, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying their pathogenic role remain incompletely understood, especially in the steroid-refractory state. Methods This study aimed to identify key biomarker genes associated with CD8 + T cell-mediated intestinal aGVHD and to characterize their expression dynamics in the steroid-refractory state. Integrative bioinformatics analysis was performed using the Gene Expression Omnibus dataset GSE79083 (a CD8 + T cell-dependent murine aGVHD model), with a human dataset (GSE134662) for independent validation. Hub genes were prioritized through protein-protein interaction network analysis and random forest machine learning. A murine aGVHD model was established for validation via clinical score, qRT-PCR, histopathology, and immunofluorescence double staining. Results Lag3 was identified as the top-ranked gene with high diagnostic discrimination. In the murine model, Lag3 was markedly upregulated in intestinal tissue of the aGVHD group, and immunofluorescence confirmed CD8 + LAG3 + T cell infiltration of the intestinal mucosa. Notably, the steroid-refractory group exhibited more severe colonic histopathological injury. In this group, Lag3 expression was significantly lower than in the aGVHD group despite persistent CD8 + T cell infiltration. A similar expression pattern was observed in the human dataset. Conclusion The reduction of Lag3 despite persistent severe tissue injury suggests that glucocorticoid-resistant CD8 + T cells may have escaped checkpoint-mediated restraint. These findings suggest a dual-pathology framework for steroid-refractory intestinal aGVHD, involving both effector mechanisms independent of LAG3 and impaired epithelial repair. Whether targeting both processes in combination would be beneficial remains to be tested.

title: Case Report: Durable complete response to dual immune checkpoint blockade and EGFR inhibition in microsatellite-stable metastatic duodenal adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Background Small bowel adenocarcinoma (SBA) is a rare gastrointestinal malignancy with limited treatment options and worse outcomes than colorectal cancer. While immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) show impressive results in mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR)/microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) tumors, microsatellite-stable (MSS) disease is traditionally considered resistant to immunotherapy. Case We describe a man in his 70s with recurrent duodenal adenocarcinoma who experienced disease progression after multiple systemic therapies, including cetuximab plus FOLFIRI. Molecular profiling by liquid biopsy showed MSS status with low tumor mutational burden (TMB = 1 mutation/Mb). Given the lack of standard alternatives, he was treated with nivolumab, ipilimumab, and cetuximab. Tumor regression was observed within 3 months, followed by a complete radiographic response in October 2022 and a complete metabolic response on PET/CT at 12 months. Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) included grade 2 adrenal insufficiency, vitiligo, and pneumonitis, all of which were manageable. At the latest follow-up in April 2026, the patient had maintained a complete response, approximately 42 months after the first documented radiographic complete response and 27 months after discontinuation of all anticancer therapy. Conclusions This case describes an exceptional durable complete response to dual immune checkpoint blockade combined with an EGFR inhibitor in MSS duodenal adenocarcinoma. Although the relative contribution of each agent and the presence of pharmacologic synergy cannot be determined from a single case, this observation warrants further investigation in prospective trials with MSS SBA.

title: Case Report: Glofitamab and intrathecal rituximab combined with ICE chemotherapy for early isolated central nervous system relapse in pediatric Burkitt lymphoma: rapid clearance and successful bridging to autologous stem cell transplantation.
abstract: Background Central nervous system (CNS) relapse is an uncommon and highly aggressive event in pediatric Burkitt lymphoma (BL), particularly when occurring early with parenchymal involvement. Despite CNS-directed chemotherapy, rapid and durable disease control remains challenging. Glofitamab, a CD20×CD3 bispecific T-cell engager, has shown activity in relapsed/refractory B-cell lymphomas, but its role in pediatric BL with CNS relapse remains unexplored. Intrathecal rituximab provides direct CNS delivery of anti-CD20 antibody. We treated a child with early isolated CNS relapse of BL using systemic glofitamab combined with intrathecal rituximab. Case presentation An 11-year-old boy with stage IV, R4-group BL involving bone marrow and CNS achieved complete remission after frontline CCCG-BNHL-2015 therapy. Three months after treatment cessation, he developed headache, vomiting, and blurred vision. Brain MRI showed multiple parenchymal CNS lesions, while bone marrow and thoracoabdominal imaging revealed no systemic relapse. CSF flow cytometry showed an abnormal B-cell population comprising 44.63% of nucleated cells, confirming early isolated CNS relapse. The patient received three cycles of ICE chemotherapy combined with glofitamab, along with seven administrations of intrathecal rituximab and four administrations of triple intrathecal chemotherapy. Glofitamab was administered with obinutuzumab pretreatment and step-up dosing, while intrathecal rituximab was combined with methotrexate, cytarabine, and dexamethasone. Neurological symptoms improved rapidly, and CSF abnormal B cells decreased from 44.63% to undetectable levels within 10 days. He subsequently underwent CNS-directed radiotherapy and autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Serial CSF flow cytometry remained negative, and follow-up brain MRI showed no active disease. The patient remains in continuous complete remission. Conclusion Systemic glofitamab combined with intrathecal rituximab may represent a feasible compartment-adapted strategy for early isolated CNS relapse of pediatric BL. Although the individual contributions of the treatment components cannot be determined because of concomitant therapies, rapid CSF clearance within 10 days enabled subsequent consolidation with autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. To our knowledge, this is the first reported use of this combination in pediatric BL with isolated CNS relapse, supporting further investigation of bispecific antibody-based immunotherapy combined with CNS-directed therapy.

originalAbstract:
Background

Central nervous system (CNS) relapse is an uncommon and highly aggressive event in pediatric Burkitt lymphoma (BL), particularly when occurring early with parenchymal involvement. Despite CNS-directed chemotherapy, rapid and durable disease control remains challenging. Glofitamab, a CD20×CD3 bispecific T-cell engager, has shown activity in relapsed/refractory B-cell lymphomas, but its role in pediatric BL with CNS relapse remains unexplored. Intrathecal rituximab provides direct CNS delivery of anti-CD20 antibody. We treated a child with early isolated CNS relapse of BL using systemic glofitamab combined with intrathecal rituximab.

Case presentation

An 11-year-old boy with stage IV, R4-group BL involving bone marrow and CNS achieved complete remission after frontline CCCG-BNHL-2015 therapy. Three months after treatment cessation, he developed headache, vomiting, and blurred vision. Brain MRI showed multiple parenchymal CNS lesions, while bone marrow and thoracoabdominal imaging revealed no systemic relapse. CSF flow cytometry showed an abnormal B-cell population comprising 44.63% of nucleated cells, confirming early isolated CNS relapse. The patient received three cycles of ICE chemotherapy combined with glofitamab, along with seven administrations of intrathecal rituximab and four administrations of triple intrathecal chemotherapy. Glofitamab was administered with obinutuzumab pretreatment and step-up dosing, while intrathecal rituximab was combined with methotrexate, cytarabine, and dexamethasone. Neurological symptoms improved rapidly, and CSF abnormal B cells decreased from 44.63% to undetectable levels within 10 days. He subsequently underwent CNS-directed radiotherapy and autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Serial CSF flow cytometry remained negative, and follow-up brain MRI showed no active disease. The patient remains in continuous complete remission.

Conclusion

Systemic glofitamab combined with intrathecal rituximab may represent a feasible compartment-adapted strategy for early isolated CNS relapse of pediatric BL. Although the individual contributions of the treatment components cannot be determined because of concomitant therapies, rapid CSF clearance within 10 days enabled subsequent consolidation with autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. To our knowledge, this is the first reported use of this combination in pediatric BL with isolated CNS relapse, supporting further investigation of bispecific antibody-based immunotherapy combined with CNS-directed therapy.

title: Low-dose dexmedetomidine adjunct to ciprofol for gastrointestinal endoscopy: a retrospective study of relative MAP reduction and rescue interventions.
abstract: Objective To examine the association of low-dose dexmedetomidine (0.3 μg/kg) added to ciprofol sedation with a patient-level mean arterial pressure (MAP) reduction of at least 20% from baseline, recorded rescue interventions, and early recovery during gastrointestinal endoscopy. Methods This single-center, retrospective, non-randomized comparative study included 100 adults (dexmedetomidine-ciprofol, n = 50; ciprofol alone, n = 50). No upper age limit was applied. In the adjunctive group, dexmedetomidine 0.3 μg/kg was administered intravenously before ciprofol; both groups received ciprofol titrated to clinical response. The primary outcome was an individual MAP decrease of at least 20% from the pre-sedation baseline, defined in the retrospective analysis plan before patient-level outcome derivation and between-group comparisons. Secondary outcomes included recorded rescue intervention, ciprofol dose, awakening time, intraoperative cardiorespiratory measures, bradycardia, hypoxemia, and other documented adverse reactions. Exploratory adjusted analyses supplemented unadjusted comparisons. Results The incidence of a MAP reduction of at least 20% was 16.0% vs. 36.0% [8/50 vs. 18/50; odds ratio [OR] 0.34, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.13-0.88; P = 0.039] in the dexmedetomidine-ciprofol and ciprofol-only groups, respectively. Recorded rescue interventions occurred in 20.0% vs. 40.0% (10/50 vs. 20/50; OR: 0.38, 95% CI: 0.15-0.92; P = 0.049). Mean lowest intraoperative MAP and mean percentage MAP reduction were similar between groups. Awakening time was 5.98 ± 1.02 vs. 6.42 ± 0.84 min ( P = 0.020); the difference was 0.44 min. Other documented adverse reactions consisted of dizziness (0 vs. 6 patients). Bradycardia and hypoxemia events were infrequent. Adjusted results were exploratory because of the limited event counts. Conclusion In this small retrospective comparison, adjunctive dexmedetomidine was associated with fewer recorded MAP reductions of at least 20% and rescue interventions, although mean hemodynamic measures did not differ materially. Awakening time differed modestly, and infrequent adverse events preclude firm safety conclusions. Larger studies with standardized monitoring and prespecified endpoints are needed.

title: A deep learning model for preoperative differentiation of uterine adenomyoma and uterine leiomyoma on transvaginal ultrasound.
abstract: Introduction To develop and validate a deep learning model for the preoperative differentiation of uterine adenomyoma and uterine leiomyoma on transvaginal ultrasound. Methods This retrospective study included 207 transvaginal ultrasound images from 98 patients between January 2020 and January 2025, split at the patient level into a training set (68 patients, 140 images) and an independent test set (30 patients, 67 images). A comparative framework was established: (1) radiomics models; (2) standard deep learning models; and (3) the proposed ResNet-50 model enhanced with the channel-aware feature modulation module. Three gynecologic ultrasonographers independently reviewed the test images for comparison with model performance. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Exploratory explainability analyses used SHAP for the best-performing radiomics model and Grad-CAM for the proposed model. Results On the patient-level test set, the proposed model showed favorable numerical performance among the evaluated models, with an accuracy of 0.833, F1-score of 0.800, and AUC of 0.855 (95% CI: 0.693-0.982). The best-performing radiomics model, Logistic Regression, achieved a patient-level accuracy of 0.667 and AUC of 0.814 (95% CI: 0.630-0.962). The proposed model showed numerically higher accuracy than the three readers. SHAP summarized the contributions of radiomic features, whereas Grad-CAM visualized image regions associated with model predictions. Conclusion The proposed model showed promising internal test performance for differentiating uterine adenomyoma from uterine leiomyoma on transvaginal ultrasound and may serve as a potential decision-support approach, warranting external and prospective validation.

title: Perioperative factors associated with delayed passage of flatus after laparoscopic uterine myomectomy: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Introduction Delayed passage of flatus (DPF) after laparoscopic uterine myomectomy may indicate slower gastrointestinal recovery, but procedure-specific evidence is limited. Methods We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 342 consecutive adult patients who underwent laparoscopic uterine myomectomy between March 2021 and March 2025. The endpoint was no documented passage of flatus within the first 3 postoperative days. Because oral-intake intolerance, nausea or vomiting, abdominal distension, and nasogastric-tube use were not systematically captured, the endpoint was treated as DPF rather than consensus-defined postoperative ileus. A three-variable logistic regression model was restricted to preoperative and intraoperative variables and interpreted as an exploratory association model. Results DPF occurred in 35 patients (10.2%). Plain radiographs in all 35 patients meeting this threshold showed multiple air-fluid levels and diffuse small- and large-bowel gas. No focal mechanical obstruction was documented after record review that included bedside abdominal findings and radiography. In the primary complete-case model (341 patients; 35 events), pre-existing constipation (odds ratio [OR] 12.84, 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.65-45.21), intraoperative intestinal adhesion (OR 39.91, 95% CI 13.89-114.71), and operative time (OR 1.014 per minute, 95% CI 1.006-1.023) remained associated with DPF after adjustment. The wide CIs, particularly for intestinal adhesion, indicated substantial uncertainty in the magnitude of association. The model had an apparent area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve of 0.939 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.894-0.978) and a Brier score of 0.040. At the data-derived Youden-index threshold, apparent sensitivity was 0.857 and apparent specificity was 0.908. A single 5-fold cross-validation yielded an area under the curve of 0.923. Discussion These center-specific findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective external validation using a multidimensional gastrointestinal-recovery endpoint.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven precision diagnosis and management of cutaneous lupus erythematosus: from lesion recognition and multi-omics profiling to clinical decision support.
abstract: Cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE) poses challenges in differential diagnosis, subtype classification, and longitudinal management because of its heterogeneous phenotypes and variable association with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). This narrative review evaluates artificial intelligence (AI) evidence by clinical task, data modality, disease relevance, and validation maturity. Direct CLE studies provide early evidence for image-based lesion and subtype classification, including a multicentre multimodal system that improved dermatologists' diagnostic accuracy. A separate proof-of-concept study used natural language processing (NLP) to estimate Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus Disease Area and Severity Index (CLASI) activity and damage scores from physical-examination notes. This text-based result should not be interpreted as automated severity scoring from clinical photographs: image-based lesion segmentation and CLASI estimation remain proposed applications. CLE transcriptomic, single-cell, and spatial studies reveal subtype-related B-cell signatures, interferon-associated keratinocyte states, specialized fibroblasts, and altered cell-cell communication; these findings are biological foundations for future models rather than validated patient-level prediction systems. Across applications, the level of CLE relevance is distinct from the maturity of validation. Current limitations include small or incompletely characterized disease-specific subsets, inconsistent image acquisition, uncertain independence of test cohorts, and limited prospective assessment of clinical utility. Progress requires transparent reporting of CLE-specific denominators, patient-level data separation, independent external validation, calibration, pigmentation-aware subgroup assessment, and clinician-supervised prospective evaluation. AI should therefore be regarded as an investigational decision-support approach for CLE, with clinical benefit established through disease-specific testing.

title: Case Report: Large ileal inflammatory fibroid polyp associated with acute intestinal perforation.
abstract: Background Inflammatory fibroid polyp (IFP) is a rare benign mesenchymal lesion of the gastrointestinal tract. Small-bowel IFPs typically manifest with intestinal obstruction or intussusception. IFP-associated perforation has been described, mostly in the setting of intussusception or as impending perforation; frank full-thickness perforation without intussusception is uncommon. Case summary A 73-year-old man presented with a 12-hour history of acute generalized abdominal pain and clinical signs of peritonitis. Abdominal computed tomography showed pneumoperitoneum without evidence of intussusception or an identifiable mass lesion. Emergency laparotomy identified an ileal perforation approximately 35 cm proximal to the ileocecal valve, adjacent to a firm submucosal mass. The affected segment was resected, followed by primary ileoileal anastomosis. Histopathologic examination showed a submucosal spindle-cell proliferation within a fibrovascular stroma with inflammatory-cell infiltration. The lesional cells were positive for CD34 and negative for CD117, DOG1, S100, SOX10, SMA, Desmin, STAT6, and cytokeratin; the Ki-67 index was approximately 3%. These findings were consistent with the diagnosis of IFP. The lesion measured 8.5 × 5.0 × 4.0 cm. The patient recovered without postoperative complications and remained asymptomatic at the 6-month follow-up. Conclusion Ileal IFP may rarely be associated with acute perforation in the absence of intussusception. Although IFP-associated perforation has been reported, preoperative identification of the causative lesion remains difficult. In unexplained small-bowel perforation, careful intraoperative evaluation may help identify an underlying IFP. Complete surgical excision is associated with favorable outcomes.

title: Evolution of colorectal cancer screening technologies and health economic evaluation: optimization strategies based on an economic gradient and dynamic risk stratification.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major contributor to the global cancer burden, with approximately 555,000 new cases and 286,000 deaths annually in China, where most patients are still diagnosed at intermediate or advanced stages. This narrative review synthesizes recent evidence on the evolution of CRC screening technologies and their health economic evaluation, with the aim of informing resource-adapted screening strategies for China and comparable settings. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and three major Chinese databases (CNKI, Wanfang Data, and VIP) were searched from database inception to 7 November 2025, with emphasis on studies published within the past five years. The evidence supports three principal findings. First, noninvasive molecular testing has substantially improved diagnostic performance: next-generation multitarget stool DNA testing achieves a sensitivity of 93.9% for CRC (versus 67.3% for the fecal immunochemical test [FIT] in the same head-to-head cohort), and stool syndecan-2 methylation testing outperforms FIT for advanced colorectal neoplasia, although sensitivity for advanced precancerous lesions remains below 50% for all currently available noninvasive assays. Second, health economic analyses consistently identify FIT as the most cost-effective primary screening tool under real-world adherence conditions, whereas structured risk-stratified and opportunistic screening models achieve higher benefit-cost ratios (9.29 for opportunistic screening versus 6.43 for population-based screening in a representative Chinese community program, although these ratios derive from a single community program, are subject to selection bias, and are not incremental comparisons). Third, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted colonoscopy-specifically computer-aided detection (CADe), as distinct from computer-aided diagnosis (CADx)-reduces adenoma miss rates in randomized tandem studies; in a single-center diagnostic study, combined AI and conventional colonoscopy showed high agreement with histopathology, although this finding derives from an enriched symptomatic cohort rather than an average-risk screening population. Most pivotal trials of emerging molecular assays were industry-sponsored, which may inflate reported performance. Building on this evidence, we propose a conceptual dual-cycle optimization framework with illustrative, author-proposed thresholds: an outer cycle that matches the population coverage of emerging high-cost technologies to regional per-capita gross domestic product and budget constraints, and an inner cycle that recalibrates individual risk annually through a four-dimensional assessment system integrating the Asia-Pacific Colorectal Screening score, serial molecular monitoring, AI-derived imaging features, and genetic susceptibility. Neither a single highly sensitive test nor a low-cost primary screening tool alone can simultaneously maximize early detection and contain health expenditure; tiered, risk-stratified, and economically graded strategies are required to reduce the CRC burden in resource-heterogeneous settings. The framework is hypothesis-generating, and its thresholds require prospective calibration before implementation.

title: Association between serum IgA levels and mortality in patients with sepsis and serum IgG ≥670 mg/dL: an observational study of clinical and MIMIC-IV cohorts.
abstract: Background The association between serum immunoglobulin concentrations and mortality in sepsis remains uncertain. This study examined the association between serum IgA and mortality in patients with sepsis and serum IgG ≥670 mg/dL. Methods Based on real-world clinical data from ICUs at two tertiary Class A hospitals in mainland China and the MIMIC-IV database, this study divided patients into IgG <670 mg/dL and IgG ≥670 mg/dL groups using a serum IgG concentration of 670 mg/dL as the cutoff. This study used comparative analysis, Cox regression, and Log-rank survival analysis to examine the association between serum IgA and mortality in sepsis patients with serum IgG ≥670 mg/dL. In addition, this study focused on nonpulmonary sepsis patients with serum IgG ≥670 mg/dL, analyzed the correlation between BALF (bronchoalveolar lavage fluid) IgA and lung imaging exudation status and duration of mechanical ventilation, and used flow cytometry to characterize the proportion of IgA1 + cells within the BALF-recovered CD45 + cell population and their IgA1 fluorescence intensity. Results There was no significant difference in serum immunoglobulin levels among patients with sepsis with different disease prognoses. In patients with serum IgG ≥670 mg/dL, each 100 mg/dL increase in serum IgA was associated with mortality after adjustment for age, sex, and SOFA score in the clinical cohort (adjusted HR, 1.269; 95% CI, 1.046-1.540; P = 0.016). The corresponding association did not reach statistical significance in MIMIC-IV (adjusted HR, 1.043; 95% CI, 0.999-1.089; P = 0.053). In patients with nonpulmonary sepsis, serum IgA concentrations and BALF IgA measurements were positively correlated with the change in pulmonary CT scores (Pearson's r = 0.5383; 95% CI, 0.2907-0.7183; and r = 0.5713; 95% CI, 0.2989-0.7576, respectively). Among patients with nonpulmonary sepsis, no statistically significant differences were observed between survivors and nonsurvivors in the proportion of CD19 + IgA1 + B cells among BALF-recovered CD45 + cells or in IgA1 fluorescence intensity within the IgA1 + B-cell population. Conclusions Serum IgA was associated with mortality after adjustment for age, sex, and disease severity in the clinical subgroup with IgG ≥670 mg/dL, but the adjusted MIMIC-IV analyses did not consistently support this association. Exploratory serum and BALF IgA measurements were associated with pulmonary CT abnormalities. These findings do not establish individual-level predictive performance or a causal role for IgA in pulmonary injury. Trial registration [https://www.chictr.org.cn] CHICTR, ChiCTR2400083751. Registered 30 April 2024.

In patients with serum IgG ≥670 mg/dL, each 100 mg/dL increase in serum IgA was associated with mortality after adjustment for age, sex, and SOFA score in the clinical cohort (adjusted HR, 1.269; 95% CI, 1.046-1.540; P = 0.016). The corresponding association did not reach statistical significance in MIMIC-IV (adjusted HR, 1.043; 95% CI, 0.999-1.089; P = 0.053). In patients with nonpulmonary sepsis, serum IgA concentrations and BALF IgA measurements were positively correlated with the change in pulmonary CT scores (Pearson's r = 0.5383; 95% CI, 0.2907-0.7183; and r = 0.5713; 95% CI, 0.2989-0.7576, respectively). Among patients with nonpulmonary sepsis, no statistically significant differences were observed between survivors and nonsurvivors in the proportion of CD19 + IgA1+ B cells among BALF-recovered CD45+ cells or in IgA1 fluorescence intensity within the IgA1+ B-cell population.

Conclusions

Serum IgA was associated with mortality after adjustment for age, sex, and disease severity in the clinical subgroup with IgG ≥670 mg/dL, but the adjusted MIMIC-IV analyses did not consistently support this association. Exploratory serum and BALF IgA measurements were associated with pulmonary CT abnormalities. These findings do not establish individual-level predictive performance or a causal role for IgA in pulmonary injury.

title: Preliminary evidence of systematic longitudinal offsets in couch corrections associated with CT localizer scan-line placement in head-and-neck image-guided radiotherapy: a brief research report.
abstract: Background Computed tomography (CT) simulation transfers external setup references into treatment planning and image-guided radiotherapy, but the effect of localizer scan-line placement relative to radiopaque markers remains uncertain. Objective This study examined associations between scan-line placement and directional differences in longitudinal couch corrections during head-and-neck image-guided radiotherapy. Methods This single-center study included 104 patients and 3,115 pre-treatment cone-beam CT records. Two operational cohorts used cranial-edge (A) or caudal-edge (B) scan-line alignment. A retrospective routine center-aligned cohort provided a clinical reference (C). The primary endpoint was patient-level treatment-course mean longitudinal couch correction (LNG), retaining treatment-system direction. Absolute LNG, events exceeding 5 mm, mixed-effects models, and an exploratory marker-visibility centroid were analyzed. Results Mean LNG corrections were -0.312, 0.625, and 0.327 mm in groups A, B, and C. The patient-level A-B difference was -0.937 mm [Bonferroni simultaneous 95% confidence interval (CI), -1.865 to -0.009; Holm-adjusted P = 0.0472]. The mixed-effects estimate was -0.930 mm (Bonferroni simultaneous 95% CI, -1.887 to 0.027; Holm-adjusted P = 0.0595). No group difference in mean absolute LNG was detected ( P = 0.5068). Each 1-mm increase in the marker-visibility centroid was associated with a 0.519-mm increase in LNG (HC3 95% CI, 0.367 to 0.671). Conclusion The evaluated workflows showed a small directional difference in pre-treatment longitudinal couch corrections, with statistical support varying across analyses. No difference in mean absolute correction was detected. These hypothesis-generating findings require further validation because scanner-operator confounding, unverified geometry, observer bias, and consent-related selection limit causal interpretation.

title: Discrimination between hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and hypertensive heart disease using deep learning-based magnetic resonance imaging.
abstract: Background Discrimination between HCM and HHD can be challenging due to overlapping imaging presentation and clinical features. This study aimed to develop a deep learning pipeline for discrimination between hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and hypertensive heart disease (HHD) using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) images. Materials and methods EARLY-MYO-HHD registry is a prospective cardiac imaging study that enrolled patients with HCM and HHD. A framework comprised of convolutional neural networks (CNN) and support vector machine (SVM) classifiers was used to estimate the probability of HCM or HHD based on CMR cine sequence and CMR parameters (including LVEF and scar size). Results A total of 368 patients were included (303 patients for model development and 65 patients for independent testing). With 10-fold cross-validation, our proposed CNN model correctly classified 88.1 ± 6.9% of patients with HCM and HHD. By combining CNN model prediction and scar size, the SVM model achieved an overall classification accuracy of 91.1 ± 5.5%, and the predictive performance showed great performance among all HCM subgroups (with or without wall thickness < 15 mm or hypertension, AUCs >0.93). Also, the CNN prediction and scar size-based model achieved a classification accuracy of 96.9% (AUC 0.99, CI 0.96-1.00) in the testing dataset. Conclusion A patient-level deep learning method was developed for HCM and HHD classification using CMR cine images. Our proposed method provided a useful approach for classification of HCM and HHD, especially in clinically ambiguous cases. Adding semi-quantitative scar size information further improved the classification accuracy of HCM and HHD patients. Clinical trial registration identifier NCT03271385.

title: TALON: a multi-task network for axillary lymph-node segmentation and source-cohort classification on breast DCE-MRI.
abstract: Purpose This study developed TALON (Target-Aware Lesion-Oriented Network) for pre-selected axillary target-node segmentation and exploratory invasive breast cancer vs. idiopathic granulomatous mastitis source-cohort classification on single-phase dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI). Methods This retrospective study included 103 patients, 104 side-specific cases, and 1,367 axial slices. Expert target-node annotations supported segmentation evaluation. TALON and a Mask-guided Multi-task U-Net were compared using five patient-grouped holdouts with 60%/20%/20% training, validation, and test partitions. Model selection, segmentation thresholds, and Platt calibration were performed using validation data. Exploratory analyses examined component removal, age confounding, and the association and predictive value of adding TALON probabilities to age. Results Mean case-level AUROC was 0.905 ± 0.047 for TALON and 0.838 ± 0.113 for the comparator; mean slice-level Dice was 0.530 ± 0.057 and 0.424 ± 0.085, respectively. Paired AUROC and calibrated Brier-score difference intervals included zero in every repeat. The training-fitted age-only mean AUROC was 0.945 ± 0.046. In post-hoc multivariable analysis, TALON probability was associated with cohort membership after adjustment for age (OR, 7.615 per SD; 95% CI, 2.795-20.748). A separate validation-fitted age-plus-TALON model achieved mean test AUROC 0.965 ± 0.022. Relative to its matched age-only model, the AUROC difference was 0.020 (95% CI, -0.015 to 0.063) and the Brier difference was -0.031 (95% CI, -0.052 to -0.009). TALON's pointing-game fraction was zero across seeds, and all paired single-seed ablation intervals included zero. Conclusion TALON supports further study of target-node segmentation and the use of complementary imaging information alongside age. The findings remain an internal proof of concept and do not establish age-independent disease discrimination, target-node-driven classification, stable superiority, nodal metastatic status, or clinical utility. Component and training-schedule benefits require multi-seed evaluation.
