title: Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography and Carotid Intima Media Thickness in Normotensive Patients with Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease and Preserved Kidney Function.
abstract: Subclinical vascular abnormalities may develop in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) prior to the onset of hypertension or kidney dysfunction. This cross-sectional case-control study compared carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) parameters in 20 normotensive patients with ADPKD and preserved kidney function, as well as in 20 healthy controls who were matched by age and sex. CIMT was measured by ultrasonography, and right-eye OCTA was used to assess macular and peripapillary vessel density, foveal avascular zone indices, and retinal and choroidal flow areas. CIMT was greater in patients with ADPKD than in controls (median, 0.6 mm versus 0.3 mm; p < 0.001). After adjusting for age, systolic blood pressure, and body mass index, ADPKD status remained independently associated with greater CIMT (B = 0.270 mm; 95% confidence interval, 0.189-0.350; p < 0.001). No statistically significant between-group differences were detected in the assessed OCTA parameters, and no significant correlations were identified between CIMT and OCTA measurements. These findings suggest the presence of subclinical large-artery structural abnormalities in this specific ADPKD population despite the absence of detectable differences in OCTA. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the prognostic significance and temporal evolution of these vascular findings.

title: Ameliorative Effect of Tirzepatide on Obesity-Induced Salivary Gland Injury in a Rat Model: Associated with Antioxidant, Anti-Inflammatory, Anti-Apoptotic, and Anti-Fibrotic Effects.
abstract: Metabolic disorders from a high-fat diet impair salivary gland integrity, and the effect of tirzepatide on these glands is unknown. We investigated tirzepatide's effects on high-fat diet (HFD)-induced salivary gland injury in rats. Forty adult male rats were randomly assigned to four groups: control (G1), HFD-fed (G2), HFD + saline (G3), and HFD + tirzepatide (G4). We assessed metabolic parameters, oxidative stress markers, inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β), caspase-3 concentration, stimulated salivary flow rate (SSFR), histopathology, and mast cell morphometry. HFD feeding caused insulin resistance and dyslipidemia, increased oxidative stress, TNF-α, IL-1β, and caspase-3 in salivary gland homogenate, histological damage to salivary gland tissue, increased mast cell indices, and collagen deposition. Tirzepatide significantly improved metabolic abnormalities and attenuated oxidative stress and inflammation, reduced caspase-3, mast cell, and fibrotic changes, and preserved salivary gland structure. SSFR showed no significant differences in pairwise comparisons. HFD-fed groups (G2 and G3) showed a reduced stimulated salivary rate per 100 g body weight (mL/15 min/100 g BW) compared with the control (G1). The tirzepatide-treated group (G4) had an improved stimulated salivary rate per 100 g BW, with no significant difference from the control (G1). The data suggest that tirzepatide ameliorates HFD-induced salivary gland injury, and this effect was associated with reduced oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokine levels (TNF-α, IL-1β), and caspase-3. The preservation of absolute SSFR despite marked tissue damage suggests that structural damage may occur without a concomitant reduction in overall stimulated salivary secretion.

title: Synthesis and Application of a Chitosan-Based AM/AMPS Flocculant for the Flocculation of Kaolinite Suspensions: Experimental and Molecular Dynamics Study.
abstract: Fine kaolinite particles form stable suspensions that impede solid-liquid separation. A chitosan-based flocculant, CS-g-P(AM-AMPS), was synthesized by ultrasound-assisted graft copolymerization of acrylamide (AM) and 2-acrylamido-2-methylpropanesulfonic acid (AMPS) onto chitosan (CS). Physicochemical characterization, batch flocculation tests, and molecular dynamics simulations were conducted with the AM/AMPS copolymer P(AM-AMPS) and polyacrylamide (PAM) as reference polymers. Characterization identified amide and sulfonate groups and a rough, porous dry-state morphology. CS-g-P(AM-AMPS) achieved higher final turbidity removal and produced larger median flocs than both reference polymers under their respective selected conditions, with a maximum removal efficiency of 98.5%. Simulations showed that the grafted polymer had the most negative total polymer-surface interaction energy and the largest interfacial hydrogen-bond population. Its segment distribution combined near-surface enrichment with extension into the adjacent aqueous phase. P(AM-AMPS) produced larger median flocs than PAM but achieved lower removal, showing that aggregate size and clarification followed different rankings. These findings suggest that extensive surface contact coupled with chain extension facilitates particle bridging and floc growth. The combined results identify CS-g-P(AM-AMPS) as an effective flocculant for clarifying kaolinite-bearing water.

title: Postoperative Periprosthetic Humeral Fractures After Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty Treated with Open Reduction and Internal Fixation: A Retrospective Case Series.
abstract: Background and Objectives : Postoperative periprosthetic humeral fractures after reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (RTSA) are challenging injuries, particularly in older patients with reduced bone stock. We evaluated the radiographic and clinical outcomes of open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) in a selected cohort and examined the uncertainty associated with humeral stem stability. Materials and Methods : This retrospective, single-centre case series comprised 12 eligible patients (nine women; mean age, 77.9 ± 7.5 years) treated with plate-based ORIF between January 2016 and October 2022 and with at least three years of documented follow-up. Four fractures were Wright and Cofield type A, six type B, and two type C. Nine stems were judged stable and three showed reproducible motion during intraoperative assessment. All stems were retained. Clinical and radiographic outcomes were summarized descriptively, with exact binomial 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for selected proportions. Results : All 12 fractures met predefined radiographic criteria for union (100%; exact 95% CI, 73.5-100.0%) after a mean of 4.0 ± 0.8 months. At a mean follow-up of 4.3 ± 0.7 years, no stem loosening, fixation failure, or reoperation was recorded. Three patients experienced complications (25.0%; exact 95% CI, 5.5-57.2%): two reported superficial incisional infections managed without reoperation and one transient radial nerve deficit. The mean Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand (DASH) score was 12.8 ± 4.7 (range, 6-20). Clinical shoulder motion was considered comparable with the contralateral side in six patients and mildly limited in six; quantitative goniometry and pre-fracture baselines were unavailable. Conclusions : In this small, highly selected series, ORIF was associated with radiographic union and satisfactory recorded functional outcomes. Three cases of intraoperative stem motion were successfully managed without exchange, but the absence of a comparator and possible indication bias preclude a general recommendation to retain a genuinely loose stem. Incomplete case-level and infection-prophylaxis information further limits interpretation.

title: Machine Learning Multiclass Models Based on Cardiac Segmentation Quantitative Parameters from Non-Contrast and Contrast-Enhanced Chest CT for the Differential Diagnosis of Acute Chest Pain.
abstract: Objectives : Acute coronary syndrome (ACS), pulmonary embolism (PE), and aortic dissection (AD) present with overlapping symptoms but require markedly different treatments. We investigated whether cardiac quantitative parameters obtained by automated segmentation of non-contrast and contrast-enhanced chest CT can support machine learning-based multiclass differentiation of these conditions. Materials and Methods : This single-center retrospective study included 628 patients who underwent triple rule-out CT angiography (147 negative controls, 193 ACS, 147 PE, and 141 AD). Twenty-six features were extracted separately from automated cardiac segmentation of non-contrast and contrast-enhanced images. Five classifiers-multivariable logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and support vector machine-were developed with a 7:3 stratified train-test split and five-fold cross-validation. Performance was evaluated by accuracy, macro-averaged F1 score, and macro-averaged area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and feature importance was assessed with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results : Multivariable logistic regression showed the most balanced performance for both modalities. The non-contrast model achieved an accuracy of 0.635, a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.637, and a macro-averaged AUC of 0.840, with class-specific AUCs of 0.814 for ACS, 0.878 for PE, and 0.887 for AD. The contrast-enhanced model achieved 0.683, 0.673, and 0.861, with AUCs of 0.881, 0.876, and 0.919. Recall for ACS increased from 58.6% to 70.7% and for AD from 74.4% to 83.7%, while AD cases misclassified as negative decreased from 11.6% to 2.3%. Left ventricular mass index and right-heart parameters ranked among the most contributory features in both models. Conclusion : Machine learning models built on automatically segmented cardiac parameters showed moderate discriminatory potential for differentiating ACS, PE, and AD. The contrast-enhanced model outperformed the non-contrast model, whereas non-contrast CT still carried complementary structural information that may support risk stratification before contrast administration.
